requirement: Constructing a MultiplePiePlot with a non-null CategoryDataset registers the new plot as a change listener on that dataset, so that a dataset change fired on that dataset after construction results in the plot firing a change event (PlotChangeEvent) to all its registered PlotChangeListeners.

KeyedObjects2D.getObject(rowKey, columnKey): after both keys are validated as present at the table level, if the specific row's backing KeyedObjects data contains no entry for columnKey (getIndex < 0), the method returns null rather than delegating to KeyedObjects.getObject(columnKey) (which would throw UnknownKeyException for such a missing cell).

In PosixParser.flatten, for a "--"-prefixed token whose long-option name IS a defined option (or, when stopAtNonOption is false, regardless of whether the name is a defined option), the token is decomposed into its name and value tokens: when the token contains an '=', the result is the name token "--opt" followed by the substring after the first '=' as a separate value token; when it contains no '=', the whole token is emitted as a single name token.

When PosixParser flatten/parse runs in stop-at-non-option mode (stopAtNonOption=true) and it encounters a plain argument token (one that does not start with '-') immediately after a recognized option that takes an argument, that token is NOT treated as the stopping point: PosixParser does not insert the '--' separator before it and does not gobble the remaining tokens; instead the token is emitted as a separate plain token so that it is consumed as that option's argument value (in parsing terms the option's value equals that token and remaining option syntax is still parsed).

renderWrappedText, when a continuation line of the wrapped text is longer than the configured width and its computed wrap position has fallen back to the end of the leading indentation padding (i.e. wrapping would only split off the padding/prefix column rather than any content), appends the entire remaining text as a final line and returns normally, instead of repeatedly re-splitting at that same padding position.

HelpFormatter.findWrapPos chops an overlong run of text at exactly column startPos+width: when no whitespace (space, '\n', or '\r') occurs anywhere in the window from startPos up to startPos+width (i.e., text there is a continuous non-whitespace run) and startPos+width is within the string (startPos+width < text.length()), findWrapPos returns startPos+width as the wrap position rather than advancing forward to the next whitespace character located beyond startPos+width.

printWrapped separates the individual source lines of a multi-line input in its output using the newline configured on the HelpFormatter (getNewLine()/setNewLine), i.e. each source line is terminated/joined with the configured platform line separator regardless of the specific line terminator sequence used to separate lines in the input.

When, after parsing, there is exactly one missing required option, the thrown MissingOptionException's message equals 'Missing required option: ' followed by the missing option's key (and is not just the bare key).

CommandLineRunner.createOptions() produces a CompilerOptions whose closurePass field is set to the boolean value of the process_closure_primitives flag; in particular, when --process_closure_primitives=false (or an equivalent false value) is supplied, options.closurePass is set to false, genuinely disabling the processing of Closure primitives such as goog.require, goog.provide, and goog.exportSymbol (the off setting is actually honored rather than being a no-op that leaves closurePass at its prior/default state).
FunctionType.hasOwnProperty("prototype") returns true: a function type reports that it owns a property named "prototype" (in addition to whatever the superclass reports).

When Compiler.init(JSSourceFile[] externs, JSModule[] modules, CompilerOptions) runs with an input array of length >= 2, every module at array index >= 1 (i.e., all but the first/root module) whose input list is empty becomes, by the time init completes, non-empty: a single synthetic source input is added to it whose source-file name is '[' + <module name> + ']' and whose source code is the empty string (so it contributes no code on its own), and that added input is included in the compiler's aggregate input set (rebuildInputsFromModules/getAllInputsFromModules and the parsed inputs).

NodeUtil.canBeSideEffected returns false for a FUNCTION node without descending into the function's parameter list or body, so a function-valued node is never considered to-have/can-be-changed-by side effects based on its internal contents; the function must be an anonymous (expression) function and a non-anonymous FUNCTION node fails a Preconditions.checkState(NodeUtil.isAnonymousFunction) assertion (IllegalStateException).

When validating an implemented interface property of a constructor type, if the implementing instance type does have the property (instance.hasProperty(prop)) but the instance property's type — after restrictByNotNullOrUndefined — cannot be assigned to the interface's declared property type (also after restrictByNotNullOrUndefined), TypeValidator emits the HIDDEN_INTERFACE_PROPERTY_MISMATCH warning at the node (when shouldReport is true) with message format "mismatch of the {0} property type and the type of the property it overrides from interface {1}\noriginal: {2}\noverride: {3}", where {0} is the property name, {1} is the property's top-most defining type as returned by the interface constructor's getTopMostDefiningType, {2} is the required (interface) property type, and {3} is the found (instance) property type.

Within a goog.scope(function(){...}) block, a reference to a name that is declared as a goog.scope-local alias (via `var name = <qualified-name-expression>`) is rewritten to that alias's fully-qualified initial value even when the reference textually precedes the alias's var-declaration statement in the block body (the full alias set of the block is discovered when the block's scope is entered, before contents are visited).

FlowSensitiveInlineVariables.process(externs, root) analyzes the program by traversing the externs root and the main AST root together as sibling roots sharing the scope rooted at their common parent, rather than by traversing the main root in isolation as its own scope root; as a side effect the externs tree is traversed within this common scope alongside the source (so free/extern references in function bodies are resolved against that scope).

When options.closurePass is enabled and dependencyOptions.needsManagement() is true, dependency management (forward-declaring provided types and re-ordering/dropping the source inputs per the managed-dependency ordering and entry points) runs during parse regardless of whether options.skipAllPasses is set; consequently, with skipAllPasses enabled, the ordered/filtered set of source inputs (as reflected in the resulting source output / input ordering) reflects dependency-based re-ordering and removal rather than the original input order.

When NameAnalyzer's FindDeclarationsAndSetters visits a class-defining call (a CALL that touches class definitions, e.g. detected via CodingConvention.getClassesDefinedByCall/ getSingletonGetter), it records that CALL as a removable ClassDefiningFunctionNode associated with the subclass name it defines, even when that subclass name has no other prior declaration/occurrence in the program and is otherwise unknown to the analyzer — thereby also creating such a name. (Previously a CALL whose defined subclass name was not already in the analyzer's symbol table was not recorded at all and thus never became a removal candidate.)

In an array-literal .join(...) call whose sole argument is the string literal ',' (equal to the join default separator), that redundant ',' argument is removed from the call (reporting a code change) before folding proceeds, so the call is folded/simplified as though no explicit separator had been passed.

The FunctionRewriter pass does not rewrite a function expression that serves as the body of an ES5 get/set member of an object literal (i.e. whose parent is a GET or SET key) into any of the helper factory calls (JSCompiler_get / JSCompiler_set / JSCompiler_returnArg / JSCompiler_identityFn), even when that function body matches the corresponding reducer's pattern (single-return this-property-get, this-property-assign, immutable-value return, or identity); such an object literal is compiled unchanged and no code change (helper insertion or replacement) is reported for it.

For an expression-statement call whose callee is a GETPROP with qualified name exactly 'goog.provide', extractClassNameIfProvide extracts (returns) the class name only when the call's first argument node is a STRING literal; if the argument is a non-null node that is not a STRING token (e.g. a variable reference, a GETPROP/qualified name, or a non-null child of some other token type), it returns null instead of extracting anything from that argument.

In CheckAccessControls.checkPropertyVisibility, any node of the form `getprop` that is the assignment target of an ASSIGN node whose first child is that `getprop` is classified as an attempted override of the property (driving the override code path: PRIVATE_OVERRIDE reported when it overrides a @private property declared in a different input file, and VISIBILITY_MISMATCH reported when the override's own declared visibility differs from the overridden property's) if and only if that ASSIGN node carries JSDoc information (parent.getJSDocInfo() != null); being in the global scope is neither necessary nor sufficient for that classification.

RenameLabels run with removeUnused=false preserves (renames to its generated name) every explicit label in the traversed tree, including labels that are not referenced by any break or continue; it does not remove or delete the labeled statements in that mode. Unreferenced-label removal only occurs when removeUnused=true (the default mode, whose behavior is unchanged).

For an unconditional jump node n that is a bare return (RETURN with no operand), a bare break, or a bare continue, whose CFG node has exactly one outgoing control-flow edge of branch type UNCOND, and which has no following sibling statement except optionally a FUNCTION declaration, the pass treats n as a useless (removable) jump exactly when the node control flow would next continue to — computed as n's computed follow — equals the single unconditional CFG destination of n; when they are equal the statement n is eliminated. Here the computed follow is the concrete statement actually flowed into from the CFG follow node after unwrapping block structure: a BLOCK follow with children resolves to its (recursively unwrapped) first child, an empty BLOCK is threaded through to its own follow, and unwrapping stops at the first non-BLOCK node (or null at end of function). A return that has a value operand is never a candidate for this removal.

A CaseInsensitiveMap treats non-null keys whose string representations differ only by character case as equal keys (equivalence used by get/put/remove/containsKey and stored-key forms), and this case-insensitive equivalence and the resulting normalized key set remain unchanged when the default Locale is switched to one with different case-mapping rules (e.g. Turkish), rather than following locale-sensitive String.toLowerCase().

SetUniqueList.subList(int fromIndex, int toIndex) returns an unmodifiable list: any mutating operation attempted on the returned view (such as via List.add/set/remove or its list iterator's add/remove/set) throws UnsupportedOperationException, so structural changes cannot be made through the subList to invalidate the parent list.

The public static method UnmodifiableTrie.unmodifiableTrie declares Trie<K,V> (the general Trie interface) as its return type instead of the concrete UnmodifiableTrie<K,V>, so client code that statically expects an UnmodifiableTrie-typed result no longer compiles unchanged.

ExtendedProperties.put(Object,Object) returns the value that was previously held under the property named by String.valueOf(key) — i.e. the raw user-store value for that key if present, else the value from the defaults (ExtendedProperties 'defaults') map if one is configured, else null.

When ZipArchiveEntry.setName is invoked on an entry whose platform is PLATFORM_FAT with a non-null name that contains no forward-slash '/', the stored name (as later returned by getName) has every backslash '\' character replaced by '/'.

TarArchiveOutputStream.writePaxHeaders constructs its PAX extended-header entry name from './PaxHeaders.X/' + the 7-bit-stripped entry name and strips every trailing '/' character from that reconstructed name before applying the header-name truncation, so the resulting PAX header entry name never ends in '/'.
UnixStat exposes a new public constant FILE_TYPE_FLAG with the value 0170000 (octal, i.e. 0xF000 / 61440), representing the mask over the 4-bit filesystem-object type indicator within a Unix mode.

TarUtils.parseName decodes each byte of the name field (up to the first NUL, or the end of the length-limited span) by appending to the result the character whose code point equals the byte's unsigned value (b & 0xFF), so that bytes with the high bit set (0x80 through 0xFF) produce characters U+0080 through U+00FF rather than being sign-extended (buggy version produced code points 0xFF80..0xFFFF for those bytes); ASCII bytes are unaffected.

TarArchiveOutputStream.getCount() (deprecated override) returns the wrapped CountingOutputStream's byte count truncated to an int, i.e. returns (int) getBytesWritten() rather than the value of the base-class ArchiveOutputStream bytesWritten field.

CSVRecord.get(String name), when the name is present in the header mapping and its mapped index is out of bounds for the record's values array (an inconsistent record), throws an IllegalArgumentException whose message is of the form "Index for header '%s' is %d but CSVRecord only has %d values!" (with name, the mapped index, and values.length substituted), instead of letting an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException propagate to the caller.

CSVPrinter.println() marks a new record (setting its internal new-record state true) so that a subsequent print() starts a fresh record without leading delimiter, even when the format's record separator is null and no separator characters are emitted.

When the adapter returned by TypeAdapters.newTypeHierarchyFactory(...).create(gson, typeToken) reads a JSON value whose decoded, non-null result is not an instance of the requested raw type (typeToken's raw type), read throws com.google.gson.JsonSyntaxException (whose message names the requested type and the actual runtime class of the decoded value) instead of returning the value.

A strict (non-lenient) JsonWriter accepts a call that writes a scalar (non-container) value directly at the root as the document's sole content — via value(...), jsonValue(...), or nullValue() (e.g. writer.value(1), writer.value("hi")) — emitting that value to the output, instead of throwing IllegalStateException "JSON must start with an array or an object."

JsonWriter now provides an overloaded value(Boolean) method: encoding a non-null boxed Boolean writes the JSON literal "true" or "false" to the underlying output, equivalent to value(boolean) with the same truth value.

NumberInput.parseBigDecimal(String) with a non-empty String that new BigDecimal cannot represent (e.g. "NaN") does not throw the JDK's raw NumberFormatException from the constructor; instead it throws a NumberFormatException whose message is "Value \"<the input string>\" can not be represented as BigDecimal". Input that new BigDecimal can parse must still return the equivalent BigDecimal value.

When a raw-write input does genuinely contain a lone first-pair (high) surrogate with no second-pair element available at end of input, so that _outputRawMultiByteChar reports the 'Split surrogate' failure, the resulting error message now takes the form "Split surrogate on writeRaw() input (last character): first character 0x<hex>" and therefore exposes the UTF-16 code unit of the offending first surrogate (rather than the previous message with no code-unit detail); this is observable in the message of the thrown JsonGenerationException.

JsonGenerator.writeEmbeddedObject(Object) called with any non-null argument that is not a byte[] throws a JsonGenerationException whose message identifies the offending object's runtime class by name (rather than only a generic fixed message); in particular it no longer succeeds for unsupported embedded object types that are not null and not byte[].

When the parser delegate is constructed with allowMultipleMatches == false, traversal stops exposing content after a single accepted match: once one match has been accepted, subsequent candidate matches encountered during the parse (matched scalar values, and matched object/array values and path-included properties, whether reached through the normal nextToken() path, the offline _nextToken2 loop, or the buffered traversal loop) are not returned by the delegate.

When resolving a polymorphic subtype, if class lookup throws an Exception other than ClassNotFoundException, the InvalidTypeIdException whose message is built as "problem: (<exception class>) <text>" embeds, as <text>, the exception's message via ClassUtil.exceptionMessage semantics, so a JsonProcessingException cause contributes its location-less original message.

Calling CreatorProperty.withValueDeserializer(deser) on a property whose value deserializer and null-value provider are the same object returns a property whose null-value provider is also replaced by `deser` (so the two remain the same object); when the property's null provider is a different object from its value deserializer, the returned property keeps that distinct null provider and replaces only the value deserializer.

When the String-collection property's ValueInstantiator exposes an array-delegating creator (via getArrayDelegateCreator/getArrayDelegateType), StringCollectionDeserializer.createContextual resolves and installs a delegate value deserializer for that array-delegate type, so that the later deserialize() call flows through the array-delegating createUsingDelegate path rather than the default-creation path.

MapDeserializer.isCachable() returns false whenever a non-standard (supplied, i.e. non-null) key deserializer is in effect, so that a Map-typed property whose keys are deserialized with a custom key deserializer does not get served by a cached MapDeserializer instance built for another property's context (the custom key deserializer is reapplied per-property rather than being reused across contexts).
Calling writeObject(null) on a TokenBuffer writes a JSON null value (i.e. a VALUE_NULL token) rather than storing null as a VALUE_EMBEDDED_OBJECT embedded token.

ObjectNode.setAll(Map<String,? extends JsonNode>) is excluded (via @JsonIgnore) from Jackson's bean-property introspection, i.e. it is no longer treated as the setter of an introspectable bean property named after the method.

Calling BaseSettings.withDateFormat with a non-null DateFormat that differs (by reference) from the current _dateFormat returns a new BaseSettings whose reported TimeZone (getTimeZone()) is the same as the original settings' _timeZone, regardless of the timezone associated with the newly-supplied DateFormat (i.e. the DateFormat's own timezone must NOT override the config-level timezone).

A BeanPropertyWriter instance can be round-tripped through standard JDK serialization (java.io.ObjectOutputStream/java.io.ObjectInputStream) without throwing (NotSerializableException or otherwise): the class now implements java.io.Serializable.

For a non-null argument, TokenBuffer.writeString(String) and writeString(SerializableString) record the appended VALUE_STRING into the buffer's output write-context (a scalar value is committed / writeValue() is applied), so that getOutputContext() afterwards reflects that a value has been written in the same way the output context of a regular JsonGenerator does after the equivalent write (e.g. an enclosing array context has its written-value index advanced); writing a null String instead delegates to writeNull and is handled through that path. The tokens/length stored are otherwise unchanged.

BeanDeserializer._deserializeUsingPropertyBased no longer lets an UnresolvedForwardReference (raised while buffering/deserializing a regular, non-creator, non-object-id bean property value) propagate as a failure: instead of aborting, it continues consuming and processing the remaining fields of the current JSON object while recording the unresolved reference.

In TypeDeserializerBase._findDeserializer, when a type id is resolved by the type id resolver (typeFromId) to a JavaType that itself already carries generic type parameters (hasGenericTypes() is true), that resolved type is kept as-is: its generic type parameters are NOT re-derived by narrowing against the base type's raw class via constructSpecializedType(_baseType, rawClass). Only when the resolved type is non-generic (has no generic type parameters) does the pre-existing narrowing to constructSpecializedType still occur.

Deserializing a Locale String whose components are separated by hyphens at both boundaries — e.g. a string with two hyphens like "en-US-foo"/hyphen variant strings — yields a three-component Locale (language, country, variant), mirroring how a two-underscore string is parsed.

For an ISO-8601 date-time with no explicit timezone indicator (reaching the branch that appends 'Z'), StdDateFormat pads the trailing time portion up to a full 12-character 'HH:mm:ss.SSS' so fully-normalized forms parse to the correct GMT instant: when less than three fractional-second digits follow full seconds, zeros are appended to reach three digits, and when the whole sub-millisecond/fraction tail is absent the literal '.000' is appended once before the 'Z'.

The JsonMappingException raised for the blocked type identifies the offending class and the reason, formatted as "Illegal type (TemplatesImpl) to deserialize: prevented for security reasons" where the parenthesized token is the actual simple class name of the blocked type.

ObjectIdInfo.empty() returns a non-null, re-usable (single shared) ObjectIdInfo whose getAlwaysAsId() is false, whose getPropertyName() is an empty/no-name PropertyName, whose getGeneratorType() is null, whose getScope() is Object.class, and whose getResolverType() is non-null (resolved to the default resolver).

In CreatorCollector.verifyNonDup, when a creator is being added to a slot whose existing creator has a different explicit status than the new one (one explicitly annotated, the other auto-detected), no conflict/type-selection logic runs and no IllegalArgumentException is thrown regardless of parameter-type overlap: if the existing creator is explicit and the new one is not, the new one is skipped (the existing explicit creator is kept); if the existing creator is auto-detected and the new one is explicit, the new explicit creator replaces/overrides the existing one.

collectAndResolveSubtypesByClass(MapperConfig, AnnotatedMember property, JavaType baseType) with a null `property` (and non-null baseType) does not fail: it skips collection of subtypes from the property's own declared subtype annotations and still produces the result based on registered types and base-type-hierarchy annotation-derived subtypes. (When a non-null baseType supplies the raw base class, a null property no longer triggers a NullPointerException at the property-subtypes step.)

In refineSerializationType for a map/map-like type, when the explicit @JsonSerialize.keyAs value Class forms a primitive/wrapper pair with the key type's raw class (and is otherwise unrelated by inheritance), refinement must NOT throw a JsonMappingException; instead it must succeed, keeping the key's raw class and the returned map-like JavaType with the key's static typing forced.

The date-format list exposed in the ParseException message thrown when parsing fails (built from ALL_FORMATS) now includes the additional timezone-less ISO-8601 format string 'yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'.

SubTypeValidator.validateSubType does not apply the AbstractPointcutAdvisor/AbstractApplicationContext superclass-name scan to an interface type: an interface whose binary name starts with "org.springframework." is not rejected by that Spring name-scan rule (it passes validation unless otherwise matched by _cfgIllegalClassNames) rather than being scanned and crashing.
A `:not(...)` selector whose parenthesized subselect is empty is rejected with an exception (the empty-argument case does not silently return the full result set).

CharacterReader normalizes its constructor input so that every carriage return, whether part of a CRLF ("
") sequence or a standalone "", is converted to a single line feed ("
"); because the normalized string is stored and used by all read operations (current, consume, matches*, consume*, isEmpty boundaries, toString), every read reflects this normalization — e.g. reading a reader constructed over "12
3" yields content "1
2
3".

Entities.isBaseNamedEntity(String name) returns true exactly when name is a known entity belonging to the base entity set (such names decode without requiring a trailing ';'), and returns false for entity names known only in the extended/full set as well as for unknown names.

Cleaning a source body whose element content is nested deeply (deep enough that the previous recursive cleaner overflowed the call stack) no longer throws StackOverflowError: Cleaner.clean(Document) and Cleaner.isValid(Document) complete on such deeply nested content instead of crashing.

When parsing XML, a bogus comment token whose data begins with `!` (content reached via `<` followed by `!` that is not recognized as a doctype, CDATA section, or regular `<!--...-->` comment, and is longer than one character) is inserted into the document tree as an XmlDeclaration node with nodeName `#declaration`, whose whole-declaration text is the input minus its leading `!`, instead of being inserted as a `#comment` node.

Element.clone() returns a clone whose lazily-derived class-name set is its own independent copy (derived from the clone's own copied class attribute), not a set shared/aliased with the source element; consequently, adding, removing, or toggling a class on the clone (via addClass/removeClass/toggleClass/classNames(Set)) does not change the set of classes the source element reports through classNames()/hasClass(String), and a class-list mutation on the source does not alter the clone's reported classes.

Parsing HTML that contains a self-closing start tag for a raw-data element (e.g. `<script ... />`) does not leave the tokeniser lexing in that element's data state, so any markup that follows it in the source is parsed normally — e.g. a `<div>` appearing right after `<script src='/foo' />` is produced as a discrete sibling element, not absorbed as raw/script text data continuing the element. Resulting DOM contains the self-closing element and normal sibling elements for the trailing markup.

When processing a non-Set-Cookie response header that occurs exactly once (values.size() == 1), the header is stored with that single value; the separately-added cases of zero or one value no longer lump multiple occurrences together as one.
When a start tag contains unrecognized input that yields an empty attribute key AND an empty attribute value (e.g. stray punctuation such as '

When the byte stream passed to DataUtil.parseByteData begins with a UTF-32 byte-order-mark (big-endian bytes 00 00 FE FF, or little-endian bytes FF FE 00 00), the content is decoded using the UTF-32 charset, this BOM override taking precedence over any explicitly supplied charsetName or any meta-tag-detected charset, so the parsing is performed on correctly decoded text.

XmlDeclaration.outerHtml()/toString() serializes the node as a complete, well-formed declaration: the opening prefix ('?' for an XML declaration where isProcessingInstruction is false, '!' where true), the declaration name, every attribute currently stored on the node (each emitted in insertion order by the standard attribute HTML serializer), then the matching closing prefix followed by '>'. Thus an xml declaration with attributes version, encoding and an extra custom attribute round-trips as e.g. '<?xml version="1" encoding="UTF-8" something="else"?>' (all attributes preserved, trailing '?' emitted); a node with no attributes renders as '<?xml?>' and not as the pre-fix malformed '<?xml>' that omitted the trailing marker.

TokenQueue.chompBalanced(open, close) no longer silently returns the partially-consumed content when it reaches the end of the character queue before the nested delimiter group has been brought back into balance (depth > 0): it now fails by throwing an IllegalArgumentException instead of returning normally.

Element.hasClass(String className) resolves the class attribute by a case-insensitive match of the attribute name to "class", so that an element carrying its class-granting attribute under any letter-casing of that name (e.g. an attribute keyed "CLASS" or "Class") is still tested against its value: hasClass returns true exactly when className appears as one of that attribute value's whitespace-separated tokens (compared case-insensitively) and false otherwise, rather than behaving as if the class attribute were absent simply because no lowercase "class" key exists.

In the InBody insertion mode's fall-through 'any other end tag' handling (used for end tags InBody doesn't treat specially), the end tag being closed is matched/used against open elements by the tag name exactly as written in the source (the case-preserved token name), so that when parsing with tag-name case preservation enabled (ParseSettings with preserveTagCase=true, e.g. ParseSettings.preserveCase) an open element whose stored tag case differs from lowercase (e.g. an uppercase custom element such as <X>...</X>) is correctly recognized and closed by its own matching-case close tag, rather than only ever being compared in always-lowercased form (as the pre-fix code did, which could not close such an element through this path).

When a consume operation in CharacterReader targets a span with fewer than one character remaining to return (an empty zero-length, or negative-length range at end-of-content), it returns the empty string "" instead of proceeding to construct a String from that (now empty/out-of-range) sub-span of the buffer, which would otherwise trigger a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. Observable through the cacheString-backed consume methods (e.g. consumeTo(char), consumeToEnd): consuming at/near end-of-content yields "" without throwing.

StringUtil.isInvisibleChar(int c) returns true if and only if the codepoint c is one of 8203 (U+200B zero-width space), 8204 (U+200C zero-width non-joiner), 8205 (U+200D zero-width joiner), or 173 (U+00AD soft hyphen); it returns false for every other codepoint (including ordinary characters and whitespace).

When parsing a 
 or  start tag in InBody insertion mode, a single line-feed character (U+000A, '\n') that immediately follows the tag in the source is consumed and discarded, so it is not emitted into the element and does not appear at the beginning of the element's text content (e.g. '
\nfoo
' parses the pre's text as starting with 'foo', without a leading newline).

Adding a header (via header/addHeader, which routes values through fixHeaderEncoding/looksLikeUtf8) whose ISO-8859-1 byte form ends with an incomplete UTF-8 multi-byte sequence whose continuation range reaches or exceeds the end of the data no longer throws an out-of-bounds exception; instead the value is accepted and stored unchanged (i.e., not treated as valid-looking UTF-8 and therefore not re-decoded to UTF-8).

A node-type test with Compiler.NODE_TYPE_NODE (an XPath node() test) is satisfied by an org.jdom Document as well as an Element (i.e., this test returns true when evaluated against a JDOM document root).

DOMNodePointer.testNode for an element node: when matched by a NodeNameTest whose local name equals the element's local name (or whose name test is wildcard with non-null prefix), and the element's resolved namespace URI is null (the DOM node has no resolvable in-document namespace binding, e.g. a namespace-unaware document), the element is additionally treated as matching that name test if the name test's prefix equals the element's literal prefix — even when comparing the test's namespace URI against the node's null namespace would not have matched.

Calling getNamespaceResolver() on a DOMNodePointer returns a cached resolver instance: the same NamespaceResolver object is returned on every call; that resolver's namespace context pointer (getNamespaceContextPointer()) is the DOMNodePointer itself, and its parent resolver is the one obtained from the superclass (the enclosing/context NamespaceResolver).

In CoreOperationRelationalExpression.compute(Object left, Object right), when after reduction left is NOT an Iterator but right IS an Iterator, the operation's result is true iff the actual relational comparison (e.g. <, <=, >, >= as given by the operation's evaluateCompare) holds between the (non-iterator) left operand as the FIRST relation argument and at least one element yielded by the right iterator as the SECOND argument; otherwise the result is false (the operand order is no longer reversed).

When a cross-tree comparison reduces both pointers to their own distinct tree roots at the same depth (both at depth 1, non-null and not equal to each other), those two roots are treated as an ordering tie and the comparison returns 0 (rather than being treated as an error).

When the right operand of an "=" / "!=" comparison (CoreOperationCompare.equal) evaluates to an InitialContext EvalContext, it is no longer collapsed to that context's single node pointer; instead the context is left in place (reset) so that the comparison iterates over the nodes the InitialContext selects, returning a match if any individual selected node value equals the left operand — e.g. a right variable holding a whole-collection/array is decomposed element by element rather than its composite value being compared wholesale against the left side.

The integer returned by translate is the number of input characters consumed, counting the optional terminating ';' only when a ';' immediately follows the consumed numeric digits: for an unterminated entity (no semicolon) the returned count omits the formerly-always-added 1, so e.g. a standalone '&#NNN' at end-of-input returns exactly its own full length; for a semicolon-terminated entity the semicolon is counted so the return is unchanged from before.

greatestCommonDivisor (the gcd calculation used during fraction reduction) treats a zero operand correctly: when exactly one of the two operands is zero, the computed gcd is the magnitude of the nonzero operand (i.e. gcd(0, x) = |x|, and returning Integer.MIN_VALUE's magnitude would be impossible), and when the nonzero companion is Integer.MIN_VALUE (whose magnitude 2^31 is not representable in an int) it throws ArithmeticException("overflow: gcd is 2^31") instead of returning a value; previously any zero operand caused the method to return 1.
ToStringStyle.isRegistered(value) returns false instead of throwing NullPointerException when the current thread's object registry is not set (i.e. when getRegistry() returns null).

When the IllegalArgumentException is thrown for an incompatible-array-type addAll call, its message is the exact string "Cannot store <array2 component type name> in an array of <array1 component type name>" (the names being the simple class names from getName(), e.g. "Cannot store java.lang.Long in an array of java.lang.Integer").

When the lower limit exceeds the string length and the effective upper limit would likewise reach or exceed the string length, abbreviate returns the whole (full-length, un-abbreviated) input string without appending the appendToEnd value, since capping lower to the string length leaves upper equal to the string length and no space is found at or beyond that index.

LocaleUtils.toLocale, when parsing an input string that has reached the country-character validation stage (a 2-char lowercase language, an underscore at index 2, and a length that passed the length guards, either ==5 or >=7) and whose character at index 3 is an underscore (the 'LL__<variant>' empty-country form), returns new Locale(language=chars 0-2, country="", variant=substring from index 4) rather than throwing IllegalArgumentException; such a string is accepted without requiring the variant portion to be uppercase or enforcing any further underscore separator.

After being serialized and deserialized, a FastDateFormat instance remains fully functional: formatting a Date/Calendar/Long produces the same output as it did before serialization, and getMaxLengthEstimate() returns the same value as before serialization.

As a result of the carry being keyed to real month lengths, a period spanning one or more complete calendar months (whose months may have differing/less-than-31 day counts) resolves into whole months plus a residual day count that is a genuine leftover within a real month, and is no longer further perturbed by a post-pass that re-normalized every field estimate by subtracting a reduceAndCorrect correction (those calls and the reduceAndCorrect helper have been removed).

When the argument to compareTo is of a different runtime class whose binary name differs from the receiver's runtime class name (a genuinely different enum type), ValuedEnum.compareTo throws a ClassCastException whose message is "Different enum class '<short class name of other's class>'" rather than returning a value.

When the pattern of a newly built FastDateParser cannot be fully consumed by the format-field grammar (i.e. trailing pattern text — such as an unterminated single-quoted literal — remains unconsumed after tokenization), constructing the parser throws IllegalArgumentException (reporting that parsing 'Failed to parse' the pattern and the index where it gave up) rather than silently building a parser for the partially-consumed pattern.

When the least-squares problem's weight matrix is a DiagonalMatrix (the standard Weight-from-array case), the square-root-of-weight computation takes a diagonal path: the weight-matrix square root held by the optimizer is itself a DiagonalMatrix whose diagonal entries are FastMath.sqrt of the corresponding shared weight diagonal — so getWeightSquareRoot() returns a diagonal matrix of element-wise square roots, and the computation/storage stays linear in the number of targets instead of expanding into a dense matrix via a full eigendecomposition (so fitting a very large number of diagonal-weighted observations no longer exhausts memory/time).

The NumberIsTooLargeException thrown by the boundary range-overflow guard reports the overflowing upper-bound value with an OVERFLOW message in its exception context and an INDEX message identifying the coordinate (dimension) whose upper−lower range overflowed.

When SimplexTableau.dropPhase1Objective scans the phase-1 objective row of non-artificial variable columns (from getNumObjectiveFunctions() up to the artificial-variable offset), it decides whether a column is a 'positive cost' column to be dropped by comparing that row entry to 0 with Precision.compareTo using the absolute comparison tolerance epsilon (this object's configured value), not a fixed ulps-based tolerance.

The off-diagonal implicit-second-derivative setup performed in prelim for the auxiliary interpolating data (case numEval > 2n+1) must complete normally instead of throwing PathIsExploredException after writing modelSecondDerivativesValues at index ih = ipt*(ipt-1)/2 + jpt - 1, so the computed nonlinear term is actually used to build the initial quadratic model.

During backward integration (target t before the current step start), in every trial-step attempt inside the local-error control loop, the step size is clamped so that the step never extends below the integration target: if stepStart + stepSize <= t, the step size is reduced to t - stepStart. As a consequence, no intermediate derivative evaluation for that trial step occurs at a time before t.

The OpenMapRealMatrix(int, int) constructor throws a NumberIsTooLargeException when the product of (long)rowDimension and (long)columnDimension is greater than or equal to Integer.MAX_VALUE, rather than constructing the matrix; dimension pairs whose product is strictly below Integer.MAX_VALUE are accepted and the matrix is built normally.

ebeDivide(RealVector v) computes, for every index i at which `this` holds a non-default entry, the quotient this[i]/v[i] into a freshly created result OpenMapRealVector, and returns it; when such a quotient falls within this vector's zero-tolerance epsilon it is dropped as a default entry, and this drop must not cause later source entries to be skipped or the call to abort with a concurrent-modification exception during iteration.

RegulaFalsiSolver (BaseSecantSolver.doSolve with method==REGULA_FALSI) never performs an objective-function evaluation at an interior anti-stagnation point: computeObjectiveValue is invoked only at the two initial bounds and at each successive Secant approximation x, never additionally from within the REGULA_FALSI update case, so the total evaluation count for a regula-falsi run is always 2 (bounds) + number of Secant iterations regardless of stagnation.

When a Regula Falsi solver (Method.REGULA_FALSI) reaches an iteration in which the computed secant approximation coincides with the current upper endpoint x == x1 (so the plain false-position update would make no progress), the solver displaces the lower endpoint x0 inward toward x1 (to a point inside [x0, x1]) and recomputes the function value there, so the bracket shrinks and the iteration can continue; consequently a regula falsi solve does not stall indefinitely with the endpoint x1 fixed and, given bracketing and sufficient evaluations, converges to the root rather than cycling or exhausting the evaluation budget at a repeat of x1.

A BaseOptimizer constructs its inherited iterations Incrementor with an initial maximal count of Integer.MAX_VALUE (rather than 0), so that getMaxIterations() reports Integer.MAX_VALUE when no MaxIter option is supplied and subclasses may call incrementIterationCount() without triggering a TooManyIterationsException solely for lack of a configured MaxIter.

equals(double, double) no longer requires exact `x == y`; for two finite, non-NaN doubles it now returns true whenever they are separated by at most one representable ulp (i.e. the same tolerance as equals(x, y, maxUlps=1)), rather than only when x equals y exactly.
After constructing with the no-arg constructor, getMaxEvaluations() returns 1000.

When assembling the current solution, SimplexTableau.getSolution() reads off the negative (extra) decision-variable column at the negative-decision-variable offset by scanning the tableau starting from row 0 (i.e. it no longer skips the objective-function rows): if a tableau run puts that column's unit (1.0) entry in an objective-function row, that row is recognized as the basic row and its RHS value — not 0 — is used as the mostNegative reference subtracted from every decision-variable coefficient when the problem is not restricted to non-negative values.

getBasicRow still returns null when the column (below the objective rows) contains more than one non-zero non-epsilon entry (i.e. the degenerate / non-basic column detection over the scanned range is retained alongside the new unit-entry requirement).

In SimplexTableau.getSolution, when multiple decision-variable columns are basic within the same tableau row, only the lowest-indexed such column is assigned the row's RHS-derived coefficient; every later decision variable whose column shares a basic row already traversed for a lower-indexed decision variable is assigned coefficient 0, so each basic row contributes its RHS value exactly once.

Line.revert() returns a Line whose point closest to the origin (getOrigin()/zero) is unchanged from the receiver's — the reverted line lies on the same geometric line and reverses only the orientation, preserving the receiver's closest-to-origin point exactly rather than recomputing it.

When handle is invoked on a mock that is the target of a pending MockAwareVerificationMode (getMock() == invocation.getMock()), the invocation causes that verification to run against the accumulated invocation data and handle returns null (short-circuit verification path), regardless of the mocked type hierarchy details of the verification mode.
Primitives.primitiveValueOrNullFor(double.class) returns a value of the double wrapper type (Double) equal to 0.0, rather than an Integer-typed boxed 0 that would fail to be used as a double.

When InvocationMatcher.captureArgumentsFrom processes a varargs invocation, the matchers occupying the vararg region are deduplicated by their underlying matcher — unwrapping MatcherDecorator instances (e.g. LocalizedMatcher) before identity/hash comparison — so that multiple matcher occurrences backed by the same actual matcher are collapsed to one; each such distinct matcher then captures the invocation's full vararg element set exactly once, never re-capturing the same elements for each repeated matcher occurrence.

Reporter exposes two-argument smartNullPointerException(Object obj, Location location) (replacing the former single-Location overload) which throws a SmartNullPointerException whose message contains, in sequence among its joined lines: "You have a NullPointerException here:", a rendering of a freshly-created Location, the string representation of the passed obj argument, "Because this method was *not* stubbed correctly:", a rendering of the passed location, and a final empty line.

Matchers.isA(clazz) reports its InstanceOf matcher and returns, as the stub/matcher result value, the default argument yielded by HandyReturnValues.returnFor(clazz): when clazz is a primitive-wrapper type such as Integer.class, isA returns a zero-valued instance of that wrapper (e.g. Integer 0) instead of null, so using isA(Integer.class) as an argument matcher for a method whose parameter is the auto-unboxed primitive type int does not throw an unboxing NullPointerException.

When building the cannotInjectDependency failure message for a passed detail exception that has no cause, Reporter.exceptionCauseMessageIfAvailable returns that exception's own getMessage() (so cannotInjectDependency reports "Also I failed because: " + that message) instead of dereferencing a null cause and throwing a NullPointerException/similar.

BaseSingleFieldPeriod.between(start, end, zeroInstance), as surfaced through concrete single-field period subclasses (e.g. Days.between / Months.between over LocalDate, YearMonth-like, MonthDay-like, MonthDayYear-like partials), returns the correct whole-unit difference between the two partials by resolving both the start and the end partial to instants against the START_1972 reference base instants (chronological ~1972-01-01 each), instead of against the chronological zero instant (ISO epoch 1970-01-01). Consequently it returns the correct count for partial pairs whose resolution against the 1970-epoch base would otherwise produce an off-by-one (dates/crossings near or spanning the epoch/leap boundary), whereas the pre-fix method returned an incorrect count for such inputs.

When ZoneInfoCompiler.verbose() is called on a thread that has never previously stored a value in the cVerbose thread-local (i.e. no prior ThreadLocal.set on that thread), it returns false instead of throwing a NullPointerException as a result of the underlying thread-local value being null.

calculatePrintedLength for a SECONDS_MILLIS or SECONDS_OPTIONAL_MILLIS field returns a length that reflects the extra minus sign that printTo(StringBuffer,...) emits for a negative combined value (i.e. it uses a one-larger baseline for negative combined values than for non-negative ones), so the computed printed length matches the actual emitted string length, including for the negative-sub-second case.
Tracer.__init__ accepts a `custom_repr` keyword argument defaulting to the empty tuple `()`, so that @pysnooper.snoop(custom_repr=...) is a valid call without raising a TypeError.
The env lookup resolves environment variable values from the controller process's ambient environment, using ansible.utils.py3compat.environ as the environment mapping.

When the Debian parser recognizes Kali (including from /etc/os-release content), it sets distribution_release to the value captured by the DISTRIB_RELEASE= line of the parsed data whenever such a line is present.

CollectionRequirement._meets_requirements treats a requirement (in any form, including an operator form such as '>=0.0.1') against an installed version of '*' as satisfied — it skips that requirement rather than attempting a version comparison — when a parent is set and the requirement is not itself '*'.

ShellModule.join_path collapses repeated/duplicate directory separators inside an argument, so a path fragment containing doubled slashes is emitted with a single separator (leading UNC double-backslash excepted).

Rhsm.subscribe_by_pool_ids passes the pool quantity to subscription-manager as a native string (converted with to_native), so a non-string quantity value (e.g. an int) appears in the command argv as its string form.
The cleanup path of `black.reformat_many` calls `executor.shutdown()` only when `executor is not None`, so a run that fell back to a `None` executor does not raise `AttributeError` during cleanup.

When BracketTracker.mark processes a leaf that is the NAME token 'for', it increases the tracker's depth by one for the tokens that follow, so that leaves between 'for' and its matching 'in' on a line are treated as being one level deeper (and thus their comma delimiters are not split on).

blib2to3.pygram exports a module-level grammar object named python_grammar_no_print_statement_no_exec_statement that is a copy of python_grammar with both 'print' and 'exec' removed from its keywords.

The `--config PATH` option of the black CLI requires PATH to point to an existing file: passing a --config value that does not exist is rejected as an invalid parameter (usage error) before any configuration-reading callback runs.

When Black splits a line, the body lines produced for imports and for function definitions whose bracketed body contains no comma token are ensured to end with a trailing comma: `bracket_split_build_line` inserts a `,` immediately after the last non-comment leaf of such a body (skipping any trailing standalone comments), so a split single-argument function definition renders its argument followed by a comma before the closing bracket.
black.Feature exposes two new mutually-exclusive members, ASYNC_IS_VALID_IDENTIFIER and ASYNC_IS_RESERVED_KEYWORD.
read_user_choice invokes click.prompt with show_choices=False (in addition to the prompt text, type=click.Choice(choices), and default='1').
APIRouter.include_router propagates each included APIRoute's response_model_exclude_defaults and response_model_exclude_none values to the newly created route.

is_scalar_field returns False for a field that satisfies the base scalar conditions (shape is SINGLETON, type is not a BaseModel subclass, type is not a sequence/collection/dict type, and the field schema is not a params.Body) whenever the field has sub_fields and at least one of those sub_fields is not itself scalar.

Constructing an APIWebSocketRoute / registering a websocket route continues to succeed with no dependency_overrides_provider configured (the provider defaults to None), and the endpoint still calls the websocket endpoint function with the solved dependency values.

APIRouter.add_api_route accepts a `route_class_override` keyword parameter (default None) and, when a non-None value is supplied, constructs the new route using that supplied class instead of `self.route_class`.

CSVLogger opens its output file through io.open(filename, mode + self.file_flags, **self._open_args), i.e. with the file object's newline translation parameter supplied by the callback rather than by the platform default.

Sequential.get_config() includes a 'build_input_shape' entry equal to the input_shape value that was passed to build() when the model was built from an explicit shape, and omits the 'build_input_shape' entry entirely when no such shape was ever recorded (e.g. a freshly constructed model, or one built only via a first-layer batch_input_shape).

sparse_categorical_accuracy accepts y_true of shape (num_samples, 1) (an extra trailing size-1 dimension) and produces correct per-sample results rather than throwing or broadcasting incorrectly; the label values are taken from the flattened y_true of shape (num_samples,), matching the shape of the per-sample argmax prediction.
keras.backend.numpy_backend defines a public module-level function in_top_k(predictions, targets, k) (previously absent from the numpy backend).
ReduceLROnPlateau's constructor accepts a keyword argument named `min_delta` (default 1e-4) in place of the former `epsilon` argument, so `epsilon` is no longer a named parameter of the signature.
keras.utils.data_utils.Sequence instances are iterable: iterating a Sequence yields its batches via __getitem__ in index order, i.e. self[0], self[1], ..., self[len(self)-1].

RNN.__call__ decides whether each of the tensors it appends as additional inputs (initial_state and constants) is a Keras tensor by using K.is_keras_tensor rather than checking for a `_keras_history` attribute, and raises ValueError when the additional inputs contain a mix of Keras and non-Keras tensors.

process_list_block, when the docstring contains no blank line ('\n\n') at or after starting_point, limits the extracted block to docstring[starting_point:section_end] (end of the section / next section heading) instead of extending the block to the end of the docstring, so text belonging to later parts of the docstring is not included in the returned block.

CentralPlannerScheduler.prune() invokes SimpleTaskState.prune on every active task on each call, regardless of whether the task is in necessary_tasks, so prune's state side effects (FAILED->PENDING retry reset when retry delay has elapsed, DISABLED re-enable when disable_persist has elapsed, and stamping task.remove when a task has no stakeholders) are applied to necessary tasks too.

Task.to_str_params() returns a dict containing an entry for every parameter the task was constructed with, including parameters declared with significant=False; no parameter is omitted on the basis of its significance.

Register.__get_reg()/Register.task_names() include every registered Task subclass regardless of whether it overrides run: a class whose run attribute is the inherited, non-overridden value is no longer omitted from the registry listing. Observable via task_names() listing such a class and get_task_cls(name) resolving it.

In Task.get_param_values, the ordered list of parameters that positional arguments are bound to consists of exactly the non-global parameters (params where is_global is False), in parameter-declaration order; global parameters are never bound from positional arguments regardless of their significant flag, and non-global parameters with significant=False are still positionally bindable.

While a task's status is RUNNING or BATCH_RUNNING, a status update to DONE, FAILED, or RUNNING is applied only when the requesting worker equals the task's worker_running; in that case the task's status is updated (and the task history is written).

Axis.set_view_interval / Axis.set_data_interval (the setters generated by _make_getset_interval for XAxis and YAxis) called with ignore=False on an axis whose current interval in the shared axes Limits object is inverted (i.e. its first entry is not less than its second entry) store the new interval as exactly (max(vmin, vmax, oldmin), min(vmin, vmax, oldmin)), where (oldmin, oldmax) is the current interval; the first (upper) entry is therefore derived from the current interval's first entry, not its second entry.

ColorbarBase.set_label(label, **kw) passes the label argument through unchanged (no str() coercion) so that non-string labels reach the underlying axis label's set_text and are converted by Text.set_text, e.g. set_label(5) yields the axis label text '5'.
Calling Axis.set_inverted on the base Axis class raises NotImplementedError (with message 'Derived must override') instead of modifying the view interval.

NDFrame.pct_change with freq=None does not apply the index-deduplication/reindex post-processing to the computed percentage change, so the returned object's index matches the (filled) input data's index exactly — including when that index contains duplicate labels, in which case no rows are dropped and no reindexing is attempted.

In init_ndarray, when the input values is not a 2D numpy ndarray (e.g. a 1-D ndarray or an existing ExtensionArray) and an extension-array dtype is in play, the resulting DataFrame has exactly one column containing those values.

IntervalDtype is importable from pandas.core.dtypes.dtypes and is imported into pandas.core.dtypes.cast so that infer_dtype_from_scalar can construct interval dtypes (Interval inference is attempted only after the period check, so a value that is both is not treated as interval).

IntervalIndex.get_indexer accepts a CategoricalIndex as its target and returns, for each position of the categorical, the same indexer value that would be returned for the corresponding underlying value (i.e. get_indexer(categorical_target) is elementwise equal to get_indexer(target) where target is the categorical's values), regardless of whether the categorical is ordered or unordered.

Index.get_value raises InvalidIndexError(key) when the values of `series` are an ExtensionArray and `key` is not a scalar (e.g. an ndarray/list of labels), rather than falling through to a numpy-based lookup of the values.

ObjectBlock._replace_coerce, when the given boolean mask contains no True entries but convert is truthy, returns a single-element list containing the block converted via convert(numeric=False, copy=True) (rather than returning the unchanged block itself).
Categorical.replace(to_replace, value, inplace=False) returns a new Categorical with the replacement applied when inplace is False, and returns None (mutating self in place) when inplace is True.
AbstractHolidayCalendar.end_date defaults to Timestamp(datetime(2200, 12, 31)) (previously 2030-12-31).

For boolean-dtype input, algorithms.diff returns an object-dtype result array (shape equal to the input, one entry per element) whose non-lag-filled positions hold Boolean values (True/False), rather than performing numeric/bool subtraction on the boolean array.
BarPlot._decorate_ticks sets the x-axis label to the index name when a name is present and use_index is True, regardless of whether user xticks were supplied.

When array_equivalent is called with strict_nan=True on object/string arrays and element-wise comparison raises a TypeError whose message contains "Cannot compare tz-naive", array_equivalent returns False (treats the arrays as not equivalent) instead of letting the TypeError propagate.

The TypeError raised by DatetimeTZDtype.construct_from_string for a matched-but-unconstructible string chains the underlying construction error as its __cause__ (err.__cause__ is the original KeyError/pytz.UnknownTimeZoneError, TypeError, or ValueError), rather than discarding it.

In array_equivalent's strict_nan=True branch for string/object dtypes, comparing two corresponding elements that are themselves array-like (e.g. lists/ndarrays held in an object array) no longer raises ValueError from an ambiguous truth value of a multi-element boolean array; the elementwise comparison is reduced to a single boolean before being used as a condition.

Block.to_native_types, in the branch where `self.is_object` is False and `quoting` is falsy, converts the (sliced) values into a fixed-width numpy unicode array whose itemsize is determined by the length of `na_rep` (i.e. `values.astype("<U{size}".format(size=writers.word_len(na_rep)))`) instead of `values.astype(str)`; the resulting array's dtype is therefore `<U` + len(na_rep) rather than `<U` + width of the longest stringified value.

_GroupBy._get_cythonized_result processes each slice through the slice's internal values (obj._data._values, i.e. the extension array backing the column, such as a tz-aware DatetimeArray) instead of the externally-exposed ndarray (obj.values); consequently, for a result_is_index=True call the gathered result is produced by indexing into that internal array, so the returned values retain the slice's extension dtype (notably timezone awareness) rather than being converted to the plain numpy dtype.

_get_grouper's label/level ambiguity validation honors the groupby axis: when the key is found in the object and validate is True, obj._check_label_or_level_ambiguity is invoked with axis=axis (the axis passed to _get_grouper), so for axis=1 a key that is both a column-level name and an index label is reported as ambiguous.

For a 1-dimensional object (ndim == 1), setting via `.at` with a tuple key of length greater than 1 assigns the value at that tuple label rather than raising: `series.at[1, 2] = 3` succeeds (and a subsequent `series.at[1, 2]` returns 3) for a Series with a single-level tuple-valued index, and `series.at[1, 3] = 5` succeeds for a Series with a two-level MultiIndex.
When DatetimeTimedeltaMixin.intersection returns the empty fast-path result (end < start), the result carries `self`'s freq (result.freq equals self.freq) rather than having a None freq.

DatetimeArray.tz_localize returns an array whose freq is None in the general case — i.e. for any call that is not one of: localizing to a UTC timezone, a length-1 array with a non-NaT value, or the tz=None-on-already-naive no-op. This includes localizing a multi-element tz-naive array to a non-UTC timezone (e.g. a 3-element daily range localized to 'US/Eastern' yields freq=None) and removing the timezone from a multi-element tz-aware array with tz_localize(None).

Because the Series derived from an Index `others` inherits the caller's index, the alignment/join branch of `cat` (guarded by `any(not data.index.equals(x.index) for x in others)`) is not entered for an Index `others` whose corresponding caller index matches, so no outer/left join is performed and the returned Series retains the caller's index.

GroupBy.quantile on a nullable integer extension-dtype column still infers an integer result, so with an interpolation other than 'linear'/'midpoint' the returned values are cast back to int64 (equivalently, output stays float for 'linear' and 'midpoint').

PeriodIndex._engine resolves its values from the index's underlying PeriodArray (self._values) rather than from the PeriodIndex object itself, so that the engine's value getter yields a PeriodArray (which exposes .view('i8') and .freq) instead of a PeriodIndex.

_wrap_inplace_method's generated in-place operators (__iadd__, __isub__, __imul__, __itruediv__, __ifloordiv__, __imod__, __ipow__, __iand__, __ior__, __ixor__) clear the operand's parent-cacher link (the attribute set via _set_as_cached) as part of the operation, so that after `s op= other` on a Series that was obtained as a cached column of a DataFrame, the parent DataFrame is NOT updated with the new Series data (i.e. a column previously dropped from the frame does not reappear).

assert_series_equal routes to the interval-specific comparison (assert_interval_array_equal on left.array/right.array) only when BOTH Series have interval dtypes; when exactly one Series has an interval dtype and the other does not, the interval branch is not taken and comparison falls through to a later dtype branch (ultimately the generic value comparison) instead of raising an 'Expected type IntervalArray' assertion from assert_interval_array_equal.

For a DataFrame-with-DataFrame flex arithmetic operation whose columns are not identical, when the operation is `**` (DataFrame.pow / DataFrame.__pow__) or the reversed `**` (DataFrame.rpow / DataFrame.__rpow__), the operation does NOT take the reindex-only-on-shared-columns path.

sanitize_array raises a TypeError with the message "Set type is unordered" when the data argument is a set (any collections.abc.Set instance, e.g. set or frozenset), instead of falling through to the catch-all cast path.

cartesian_product no longer coerces factors through pandas.core.common.values_from_object (the `import pandas.core.common as com` dependency is removed and the function still works for all supported inputs).
For a Series with a string ('abc') object index, ser.at[0] and ser.loc[0] raise KeyError matching '^0$' rather than a TypeError about label indexing.
In Categorical.replace, when the replacement value for a matched category is NA, that category is removed (its values become missing) and any remaining replacements are still processed.
Rolling.corr(pairwise=...) on a dimension-1 object whose window is an offset (freq-type) rolling window does not select `self._get_window(other)`; the frequency-based window value is used instead.
In get_grouper, when the is_in_obj(gpr) predicate evaluates `obj[gpr.name]` and that lookup raises ValueError, the predicate returns False rather than propagating the ValueError.
Block.setitem raises a ValueError when the passed indexer is an np.ndarray whose ndim exceeds the block's own ndim, instead of proceeding to attempt the assignment.

When get_handle wraps an input file object in a TextIOWrapper, the newly created wrapper is not appended to the returned handles list if the underlying object is itself a BufferedIOBase or RawIOBase (only the wrapper for other kinds of objects is registered there).

When shift pads with the explicit Interval fill_value, only min(abs(periods), len(self)) pad entries are produced, so if abs(periods) exceeds len(self) the result length still equals len(self) and all entries equal fill_value.

For scalar .at access, an integer key on an axis that is neither integer-holding nor floating (e.g. an object/string index) still raises ValueError with the message 'At based indexing on an non-integer index can only have non-integer indexers'.

When a non-scalar aggregation result is cast back to the calling column's extension-array dtype, the cast-back is performed only if the result is non-empty and its first element is an instance of the extension dtype's scalar type; otherwise the result is returned unchanged with its naturally inferred dtype instead of being converted to the extension array type.
Constructing a TimedeltaIndex from an existing TimedeltaArray with freq=None (the default) returns an index whose freq equals the input TimedeltaArray's freq, preserving the fast-path behavior.

_Concatenator._get_comb_axis passes the concatenator's copy flag (self.copy, set from the concat(copy=...) argument) through to get_objs_combined_axis, so pd.concat(copy=True) results in a copied non-concatenation axis index while pd.concat(copy=False) does not.

The unstacked result of unstacking on a tuple-valued level name keeps the tuple names intact as level names: the levels that were not unstacked appear as the result's index name(s) and the unstacked tuple name appears as the name of the new column level (e.g., unstacking ("A", "a") from names [("A", "a"), ("B", "b")] yields an index named ("B", "b") and columns with a level named ("A", "a")).

The TypeError raised by TimedeltaIndex.searchsorted for an incompatible value carries the message "searchsorted requires compatible dtype or scalar, not {type(value).__name__}" (the offending value's type name is interpolated).

pandas.core.indexes.datetimelike exposes the names DatetimeArray and TimedeltaArray, imported from pandas.core.arrays (so that DatetimeIndex/TimedeltaIndex underlying arrays can be tested with isinstance against those classes inside this module).

For two fast-unionable TimedeltaIndex objects where self's first element is greater than other's first element, calling left.union(right, sort=False) returns an index whose values are self's values followed by exactly those values of other that are strictly less than self's first element (the overlap is removed), preserving the original element order rather than returning a sorted result.

An allowed_domains entry that looks like a URL is not included in the compiled host regex (its escaped text is absent from the pattern), so requests to that URL's literal text subdomain do not match via that entry.

For a Location header given as bytes that encode non-ASCII characters, the resulting redirected request URL percent-encodes those bytes using their raw byte values (so latin1-encoded '/ação' -> 'a%E7%E3o' and UTF-8-encoded '/ação' -> 'a%C3%A7%C3%A3o'), rather than percent-encoding UTF-8 of the latin1-decoded code points.
is_gzipped(response) matches the Content-Type value case-insensitively, so values such as 'Application/GZip' or 'APPLICATION/X-GZIP' return True.

The Content-Disposition header value is decoded as latin-1 with undecodable/invalid bytes replaced, so arbitrary byte sequences (e.g. b'.doc' with high-bit bytes) map to a Response class instead of propagating a UnicodeDecodeError; non-ASCII bytes in the filename are decoded via latin-1 rather than failing or being silently dropped.
WrappedRequest exposes a read-only attribute-style property 'host' that returns the netloc of the wrapped request's URL (same value as get_host()).
When a LocalCache has a falsy limit (None or 0), assigning items never evicts entries, so the number of stored keys grows without bound (all assigned keys remain retrievable).

HttpProxyMiddleware._get_proxy encodes the 'user:password' credential string (both parts URL-unquoted when needed) into bytes before base64-encoding it, so the returned creds value is a bytes object equal to base64.b64encode(<bytes of 'user:pass'>).strip() rather than a base64 of a py2-str.

A proxy CONNECT response delivered as a bytes object whose status line matches 'HTTP/1.x 200' is recognized by the response matcher, so the tunnel is established: the transport is switched to TLS and the endpoint's tunnel-ready deferred is called back with the protocol (instead of the match raising a str-pattern-on-bytes TypeError).

WrappedRequest.get_header returns the header value converted to a native string using error replacement, so a header value whose bytes are not valid UTF-8 yields a string with the undecodable bytes replaced (U+FFFD) instead of raising a UnicodeDecodeError.

CrawlerProcess.__init__ passes the instance's normalized settings object (self.settings, a Settings instance) to configure_logging, so that a falsy/empty dict argument does not cause the root-logger handler setup inside configure_logging to be skipped (and so configure_logging never receives a raw dict from CrawlerProcess).
The ValueError raised by Response.follow(None) is a plain ValueError (matching the check/raise semantics implemented in the patch).
When the namespace passed to ItemMeta.__new__ does not contain '__classcell__' (classcell is None), no '__classcell__' key is added to the namespace of the constructed class.
For a given pipeline component, values supplied as load-time overrides take precedence over the corresponding values found in meta['pipeline_args'][component_name] when both define the same key.

Class wiki_entity_linking.wikipedia_processor / method _process_wp_text: when no text body matching the `<text>...</text>` region can be found in the accumulated article text, the method returns (None, None).

The per-component configuration passed to the non-.pipe component in Language.evaluate is the component's entry from component_cfg, with batch_size defaulted to the evaluate batch_size argument, i.e. identical to the kwargs used for the .pipe branch.

In pip_unknown_command.get_new_command, the suggested command name is extracted from output text matching `maybe you meant "..."` by taking the entire quoted token (any characters except a double quote), so a suggestion containing non-[a-z] characters is captured in full rather than only its leading [a-z] prefix.

When the split command parts contain the standalone token '--set-upstream', git_push.get_new_command builds the corrected command from the command script with that token and the single token immediately following it removed.

For a git/hub command whose stderr contains the substring "did not match any file(s) known to git.", the git_add rule's match() returns True even if stderr does NOT contain "Did you forget to 'git add'?" (the modern-Git stderr form without the add hint).
When the command script has at least two whitespace-separated tokens, git_fix_stash.match returns True iff the second token equals 'stash' and command.stderr contains 'usage:'.

The `cache`-decorated function (`thefuck.utils.cache`'s `_cache` wrapper) uses `contextlib.closing(shelve.open(cache_path))` as the `with` block's context manager, so the database returned by `shelve.open` is closed (its `close()` method called) when the cache read/write block exits, rather than requiring the shelve object itself to implement the context-manager protocol.

When the script uses a longer launcher accepted by match ('xdg-open', 'gnome-open', 'kde-open'), get_new_command preserves that launcher verbatim and inserts 'http://' after it, e.g. 'xdg-open github.com' yields 'xdg-open http://github.com' (the launcher is not truncated or rewritten to 'open').

Fish.info() determines the shell version by invoking a single subprocess with the argument list ['fish', '--version'] (with stdout captured and stderr discarded), rather than running `fish -c 'echo $FISH_VERSION'`.
ls_lah.match returns True when command.script is exactly 'ls' (no trailing space or arguments).

When an upstream option ('--set-upstream' or '-u') is present in command.script_parts at an index, get_new_command removes the argument at that index (the option itself) and then attempts to remove the element now occupying that same index; if that second removal fails because the index is out of range, it is silently ignored rather than propagating an IndexError.

WaitIterator.next() registers a done-callback on the Future it returns (the running future) that holds a strong reference to the WaitIterator, so that the WaitIterator is not garbage-collected while that returned future is still pending even when the caller retains no other reference to it.
tqdm defines a Python-2 compatible `__nonzero__` method whose result is identical to `__bool__` (delegates to __bool__), so boolean coercion works the same on Python 2 and Python 3.

format_sizeof promotes a value to the next SI unit postfix before its fixed-point rendering could display four (or more) digits in the current unit: e.g. format_sizeof(999.99) yields '1.00K' (not '1000'), and format_sizeof(999.99, suffix='B') yields '1.00KB'.

For a bare unary filter part `key` (no comparison operator) whose value in the dict is a boolean, _match_one returns True only when the value is True and returns False when the value is False — i.e. a boolean field with value False no longer passes the bare form even though it is not None.

urljoin does not treat a path as an absolute URL when its leading scheme-like prefix is not a syntactically valid scheme (e.g. starting with a digit or containing invalid scheme characters), so such paths fall through to the base-relative joining logic.

YoutubeIE._extract_chapters_from_json returns a falsy value (None) without raising when no JSON chapter data can be obtained from the webpage: the webpage is missing/empty, the RELATED_PLAYER_ARGS JSON is absent or unparseable, the parsed player object is not a dict, the watch_next_response entry is absent or not a string, the parsed watch_next_response is not a dict, or the nested chapter list is absent/empty.

js_to_json still treats an 'e' or 'E' that is not immediately preceded by a digit as an identifier token and quotes it, so a standalone bare 'e'/'E' occurrence (e.g. a property value of e) is emitted as the double-quoted string "e"/"E" as before.
dfxp2srt returns a unicode (compat_str) object containing the converted SRT data.

Escaped `%%` and `$$` sequences present in the output template are not consumed by the pre-substitution expansion step: `%%` in the template yields a literal single `%` in the returned filename (e.g. outtmpl `%%(height)06d.%(ext)s` returns `%(height)06d.mp4`), and `$$` in the template survives the expansion step unaltered.

Within a quoted operand, the enclosing quote character may be escaped with a backslash (e.g. 'description = "a\"b"'), and the escaped sequence is unescaped in the comparison value (\" becomes " and \' becomes ').

js_to_json converts the string content of a JavaScript string literal back to numeric form only when that content is entirely a hex or octal numeral (with optional trailing whitespace/colon); otherwise the literal is preserved/returned as a quoted string rather than being truncated to a numeric prefix (e.g. input content '07777abc' stays the string "07777abc" instead of becoming 4095).

_htmlentity_transform returns the literal string '&<entity>;' when the entity matches the numeric-reference form (#<digits> or #x<hexdigits>) but its codepoint is not a valid character (e.g. '&#2013266066;' yields '&#2013266066;'), instead of letting the chr() conversion's ValueError propagate (so unescapeHTML does not raise on such input).

parse_duration accepts a string consisting solely of a number followed by a minutes unit ('min', 'mins', 'minute', 'minutes', case-insensitive) and returns that number of minutes converted to seconds (value * 60, e.g. '10 mins' -> 600.0), rather than returning None.
youtube_dl.utils exposes a function named fix_xml_ampersands(xml_str) that takes an XML string and returns a string.
url_basename returns u'' (rather than raising or returning None) for input URLs that do not match the pattern (no '//' host followed by a path).

YoutubeDL.build_format_selector accepts a format specification that combines a '/' choice with a top-level ',' list at the same nesting level (e.g. 'bestvideo/best,worst') and returns a usable format-selector function without raising an error.

For a mixin column (an object whose info descriptor derives from MixinInfo), reading info.groups yields a read-only ColumnGroups bound to that column (constructed from the column itself); grouping the containing table therefore makes aggregation of the mixin column operate over the table's groups.

For a masked structured (record) array whose dtype includes one or more fields whose values are themselves multi-element sub-arrays (a field dtype carrying a non-scalar shape), string formatting (np.array2string / array_str / repr / str) renders the sub-array contents in full, with each masked inner position displayed using the same masked placeholder applied to masked plain scalar cells rather than the raw unmasked value, and completes without error.
Calling/set_enabled_constants with any modname other than the supported 'astropyconst13' raises ValueError with a message naming the unsupported modname, before any constant values are changed.
