On SQLite, evaluating LPAD, REPEAT, or RPAD with any NULL argument (e.g. a NULL text or NULL length arising from a NULL column) returns NULL rather than raising a user-defined-function error, so text functions using those build NULL results for NULL inputs.

An app-label argument that refers to an app which is installed in INSTALLED_APPS but has no migrations is no longer treated as an error: validation only rejects labels that fail apps.get_app_config (non-installed), so such an installed-but-unmigrated app no longer causes the process to raise an error or exit non-zero for that reason.

For a non-add object change with non-empty changed form data, the returned change_message's top-level {'changed': {'fields': [...]}} entry must list each changed form field by its verbose label rather than its raw attribute name — each label being the corresponding form field's .label, with the raw field name used when that field has no (empty) .label or is not present as a field on the form.

Preparing a value containing an aggregate expression for an INSERT raises FieldError whose message is 'Aggregate functions are not allowed in this query (fieldname=value).' — i.e. it ends with an interpolation of the target field's name and the resolved expression, rather than the bare 'Aggregate functions are not allowed in this query'.

A new backend capability flag features.supports_frame_range_fixed_distance is introduced: it defaults to False on the base BaseDatabaseFeatures (so most backends report False), while the Oracle backend (DatabaseFeatures.supports_frame_range_fixed_distance) is declared True, advertising that Oracle supports RANGE window frames at a fixed non-None distance.

When USE_TZ is enabled and the requested timezone name differs from the connection timezone and encodes a fixed offset via an inline '+' or '-' sign (a datetime.timezone-style name), the CONVERT_TZ target argument is reduced to just the signed-offset tail starting at that sign (e.g. 'UTC+05:00' -> '+05:00', sign kept as written), rather than passing the full name, so that MySQL interprets the fixed Unicode offset; datetimes converted to a fixed-offset timezone thereby reflect that nominal offset. Names lacking such an inline sign are used unchanged.

When register() is called on a model that is already in the registry and whose existing registration entry's admin object string representation ends with '.ModelAdmin' (i.e. the model was registered with a plain default ModelAdmin), it raises AlreadyRegistered whose message is exactly "The model <ModelName> is already registered in app '<s>'. " where <s> is that string representation with the trailing '.ModelAdmin' removed (e.g. the plain ModelAdmin's module path such as django.contrib.admin.options).

For each unresolvable custom error handler, the emitted urls.E008 Error's message exactly equals "The custom handler{status_code} view '{path}' could not be imported.", where status_code is the numeric handler code (400/403/404/500) and path is the string value stored in the urlconf module's handler{status_code} attribute at the time of the failure.

In page_not_found, when the default 404.html template is unavailable (TemplateDoesNotExist for the default template name), the returned HttpResponseNotFound body is a complete HTML5 document that starts with '' and ends with '', with a containing "Not Found" and a containing "

Not Found

" followed by a

whose text is 'The requested resource was not found on this server.'

AutoField.get_prep_value, when the value passed after super().get_prep_value is not None and not an OuterRef and cannot be converted by int(value), raises an exception of the same class as the one int(value) raised (TypeError or ValueError), whose message is "Field '%s' expected a number but got %r." % (self.name, value), with the original conversion error chained via 'from e'.

In generated compound SQL, the per-operand parenthesization that is otherwise applied when the backend feature supports_slicing_ordering_in_compound is enabled is emitted only when the compound query is not itself a nested subquery: when a combined query is rendered as the subquery of an enclosing query (self.query.subquery is True), its top-level combined operands are not additionally wrapped in parentheses that a standalone combined query on such a backend would receive.

QuerySet.query is exposed as a lazily-evaluated attribute whose read returns the queryset's underlying SQL Query; if the queryset holds a pending deferred filter (captured from an earlier filter()/exclude() made while the queryset was set to defer its next filter), the first read of .query applies that pending filter in-place to the underlying query and clears it, so later .query reads and all downstream operations see it applied exactly once (never skipped, never duplicated).

django.views.debug.technical_500_response now selects its response body format by Accept-header content negotiation: if request.accepts('text/html') it returns an HTML traceback with content_type='text/html' and status_code; otherwise it returns a plain-text traceback with content_type='text/plain; charset=utf-8'. The choice no longer depends on the X-Requested-With (is_ajax) header.
ManifestFilesMixin's constructor accepts a keyword argument manifest_storage and stores it on the instance as the manifest_storage attribute.

When django.forms.models._get_foreign_key is called with no fk_name and the model has more than one ForeignKey to parent_model (i.e. the pathological over-disambiguation case), the ValueError it raises now has the full message: “'<model._meta.label>' has more than one ForeignKey to '<parent_model._meta.label>'. You must specify a 'fk_name' attribute.” — i.e. the message appends the guidance sentence "You must specify a 'fk_name' attribute." to the pre-existing prefix.

Options.total_unique_constraints returns the list of objects in Meta.constraints that are UniqueConstraint instances whose condition attribute is None (i.e., unconditional/total unique constraints); UniqueConstraint instances with a non-None condition (partial constraints) and constraint objects that are not UniqueConstraint instances (e.g. CheckConstraint) are excluded from the returned list.

When make_password raises TypeError for a non-bytes/str, non-None password, the exception message uses the __qualname__ of the passed password's type in the text 'Password must be a string or bytes, got <qualname>.'

Every call to django.conf.urls.url(regex, view, kwargs=None, name=None) emits a deprecation warning whose category is RemovedInDjango40Warning (a subclass of PendingDeprecationWarning) and whose message text is 'django.conf.urls.url() is deprecated in favor of django.urls.re_path().'

When autodetection changes an already-existing (kept) model whose `order_with_respect_to` option changes and which simultaneously has index/unique/index_together/constraint/db-table changes to emit, the `AlterOrderWithRespectTo` operation for that model is generated (and therefore ordered) before the added-index, altered-unique-together, altered-index-together, added-constraint, and altered-db-table operations belonging to the same autodetection run, so schema referencing the ordering's `_order` column is not added ahead of the ordering operation.

When the state for a model instance is produced by Model.__getstate__, FK/related-value entries already present in the source instance's ModelState.fields_cache are carried over as copied entries into the returned state's copied fields_cache (rather than being dropped or shared by reference), so a shallow copy or unpickled copy of an already-populated instance retains its prior cached related values independently of any later mutations to the original's cache.

When deletion via Collector.collect is blocked by protected foreign keys and it aggregates references into a ProtectedError, the raised exception's `protected_objects` attribute (and the second positional element of its `args` tuple, which is what its repr renders) is a materialized `set` of the referencing objects — never a lazy iterator such as an `itertools.chain` — so the attribute is directly inspectable/iterable and each distinct referencing object appears once.

In BaseFormSet.management_form, when the formset is bound and the submitted ManagementForm is invalid, the raised ValidationError (code 'missing_management_form') carries a message that begins with 'ManagementForm data is missing or has been tampered with' followed by a suffix 'Missing fields: <names>', where <names> is the comma-and-space joined list of form.add_prefix(field_name) applied to each field that appears in form.errors.

Constructing django.core.cache.backends.memcached.MemcachedCache (calling MemcachedCache(server, params)) emits a RemovedInDjango41Warning whose message states that MemcachedCache is deprecated in favor of PyMemcacheCache and PyLibMCCache.

django.utils.version no longer defines the module-level constants PY36 and PY37 (the minimum supported Python is now 3.8); third-party code that did 'from django.utils.version import PY36/PY37' will get an ImportError, while PY38 (and PY39) remain available.

django.db.models.fields.related.RelatedField.deconstruct() emits a `related_query_name` entry in its returned kwargs equal to the related_query_name value originally supplied to the field's constructor (snapshotted at construction in self._related_query_name), independent of any later change to remote_field.related_query_name, and omits the key when none was originally supplied.

When LocaleMiddleware.process_response() issues the 'add missing language prefix' redirect (404 response, no language prefix in path, i18n_patterns in use with modified/prefixed default language, and the language-prefixed URL or its trailing-slash variant is valid), the returned redirect response carries a Vary header that includes both 'Accept-Language' and 'Cookie' (in addition to any Vary fields already present on the redirect).

When migration_plan triggers the replaced-migration recovery path described above, it recomputes the plan from scratch over the entire targets sequence (preserving the caller's clean_start) against the replacements-disabled graph, so the returned plan correctly covers all requested targets rather than being a partial continuation of the interrupted loop.

When a concrete (DB column-bearing) Field is contributed to a model class, the field's attribute access (descriptor) is always installed on that model class regardless of whether the same-named attribute is already present on or inherited by the model, so the field's attribute takes precedence over (shadows) any pre-existing colliding class-level attribute (method, classmethod, or property/data-descriptor inherited from a base, e.g. an abstract model).

Every concrete cache-operation entry point across the db, dummy, filebased, locmem, and memcached backends (add/get/set/touch/delete/delete_many/has_key/incr/get_many/set_many and DatabaseCache.get_many key mapping) continues to produce a made key and subject that made key to the backend's key-validity check before performing the operation — the same observable warning/error behavior on invalid keys, now routed through make_and_validate_key.

When floatformat is given a string argument ending in the letter 'u' without a preceding 'g' (e.g. '2u', '-3u', 'u'), the formatted result is unlocalized: it uses the default '.' decimal separator and non-locale thousand separator rather than the active locale's separators. E.g. with the pl locale active, 66666.6666|floatformat:"2u" yields "66666.67". (Previously such an argument failed arg parsing and returned the repr of the input.)

prepare_lookup_value' accepts an optional third argument `separator` (defaulting to `','`); when the lookup key ends with `__in`, it splits the value string into a list on that separator instead of a hard-coded comma (e.g. prepare_lookup_value('x__in', 'a;b', ';') returns ['a','b']), so callers not supplying a separator still get the previous comma-splitting behavior and the __isnull handling is unchanged.

When QuerySet.bulk_update is called updating a relation field, and some object in `objs` has that relation cached to an unsaved related object (pk is None), bulk_update raises ValueError with message 'bulk_update() prohibited to prevent data loss due to unsaved related object '<field>'.' instead of silently persisting a null/stale key for that field.
The migrate management command accepts a --prune command-line option (stored as the 'prune' option).

remove_non_capturing_groups(pattern) returns the input URL-regex pattern with each top-level non-capturing group (?:...) removed entirely — its '(?:' opening marker, its balanced matching ')', and all text between them are dropped, while all other text outside such groups is preserved in place — and this holds regardless of where the non-capturing group is located in the pattern (at the start, interior, or end) and regardless of whether its content itself contains further nested groups (which are removed along with the enclosing group). E.g. '^(?:\w+)a' -> '^a'; '^a(?:\w+)/b(?:\w+)' -> '^a/b'; '^(?:\w+(?:\w+))a' -> '^a'; '(?P<a>\w+)/b/(?:\w+)c(?:\w+)' -> '(?P<a>\w+)/b/c'; a pattern with no non-capturing group is returned unchanged.

When get_normalized_value (reached by related filters such as exact and __in over a relation, e.g. MyModel.objects.filter(rel=unsaved_instance)) is passed a model instance whose pk attribute is None (an unsaved instance), Django raises a RemovedInDjango50Warning deprecation warning bearing the exact message "Passing unsaved model instances to related filters is deprecated.".

When BaseHandler.adapt_method_mode adapts a synchronous method for an async mode (is_async=True and method_is_async=False) with debug=True, it emits a DEBUG record on the 'django.request' logger whose formatted message is 'Synchronous handler adapted for {name}.'.

When HttpResponseBase.set_cookie is called with an 'expires' argument that is a datetime.datetime object (a naive datetime interpreted as UTC, or an aware datetime in any time zone) together with a non-None 'max_age' argument, it raises ValueError with message "'expires' and 'max_age' can't be used together." rather than silently computing max_age from expires and discarding the caller-supplied max_age.

URLField.to_python (and therefore URLField.clean) prepends the field's configured scheme (self.assume_scheme) rather than a hard-coded 'http' to scheme-less URL inputs, so the scheme prepended to a scheme-less value such as 'example.com' is whatever scheme the field was constructed with.

Constructing a Paginator without a supplied error_messages (or with error_messages=None) sets the instance's error_messages attribute to the default_error_messages dict, so the resulting Paginator error_messages always contains the three keys invalid_page, min_page, and no_results.

When _save_parents re-encounters, along a second inheritance branch, a concrete parent that was already saved during the same save, the prior outcome for that parent (inserted vs. not) is reused so that a shared ancestor which had been inserted is still reported as having inserted parents (keeping the cumulative 'a parent was inserted' result true for the recursion), rather than losing knowledge of that earlier insert.

When converting a grayscale string specification, matplotlib.colors.to_rgba (via _to_rgba_no_colorcycle) raises a ValueError if the string parses to a float value outside the inclusive range [0, 1], instead of returning an RGBA tuple whose R/G/B components lie outside that range. The raised error message identifies the offending input as an invalid string grayscale value and states that the value must be within the 0-1 range (e.g. the message contains "Invalid string grayscale value" and "Value must be within 0-1 range").

matplotlib.pyplot.switch_backend, when called with a requested backend whose (exact string) name differs from the currently set rcParams['backend'] value, closes all open figures (destroys/removes all figure managers via close('all')) after switching to the new backend.
RcParams.copy() returns a new RcParams instance (not a plain built-in dict) that holds the same key→value pairs as the source RcParams.

ContourSet.find_nearest_contour(x, y, indices=None, pixel=True) raises ValueError (carrying the message "Method does not support filled contours.") when invoked on a filled ContourSet (self.filled is True), regardless of the value of the indices argument.

If eventplot is given an array-like alpha whose length (other than a broadcastable single-element value) differs from the number of position sets, eventplot raises ValueError with message 'alpha and positions are unequal sized sequences'.

Text._get_layout computes the layout (bounding box, per-line metrics/parts, and descent) from the wrapped text returned by _get_wrapped_text() rather than from the raw stored text, so that when wrap=True (and usetex is False) the extent/reservation it reports reflects the wrapped multi-line rendering instead of a single long line — for wrapping widths that actually trigger one or more breaks. This makes all consumers of _get_layout (the returned bbox/info used, e.g., by get_window_extent and the layout-time tightbbox/constrained-layout paths that call _get_layout before draw) report the same, wrapped shape that draw renders.

imsave raises a ValueError (with a message indicating the format does not support metadata) instead of silently ignoring *metadata* when saving to any raster format handled by Pillow other than 'png' (e.g. jpeg, tiff, webp); metadata continues to be honoured for 'png' and for the vector formats 'pdf'/'ps'/'eps'/'svg', and a None metadata still passes through unchanged.

Calling grab_frame(savefig_kwargs=...) where savefig_kwargs contains the key 'dpi', 'bbox_inches', or 'format' raises a TypeError (rejected before the frame is saved), because those arguments are controlled by the MovieWriter.

The width of the marker-edge strokes on the PathCollection returned by Axes.scatter is drawn from one unified driver regardless of spelling: whether supplied via the explicit plural parameter `linewidths`, or via the singular collection-alias keyword `linewidth`, and combining both forms, the value is resolved through Collection keyword normalization so that the final edge-stroke width is deterministic and matches the collection's resolved linewidth semantics.

AnnotationBbox.get_tightbbox can be called without an explicit renderer (renderer=None); it then uses the owning Figure's default renderer, so that placement update and child tightbbox queries are performed against a valid renderer.

When a scatter-plot is drawn with a point-estimate aggregation (i.e. x_estimator or x_bins is in effect, so per-x estimate points plus vertical confidence-interval bars are rendered) and an alpha value is supplied in the scatter keywords (e.g. via regplot/lmplot scatter_kws), the vertical confidence-interval error-bar lines drawn at each estimate point are rendered with that same alpha rather than with their previous full-opacity default.

Mounting a prefix with Session.mount replaces the previously registered adapter for that exact prefix if one exists, updates that adapter's value in place, and still keeps every mounted adapter (including that remounted prefix) reachable for dispatch, so the registry always contains one entry per distinct prefix with the latest-mounted adapter winning for that prefix.
merge_hooks(request_hooks, session_hooks) returns request_hooks unchanged as the merged result whenever session_hooks is None or session_hooks has an empty list ('[]') for the 'response' event.

HTTPAdapter.send catches a urllib3 ClosedPoolError raised by the connection operation and re-raises it as a requests.exceptions.ConnectionError (constructed from the original exception with request=request), rather than letting the raw urllib3 exception escape to the caller.

requests.exceptions defines a new exception class InvalidProxyURL, subclassing InvalidURL (and thus RequestException/ValueError), so that code can `from requests.exceptions import InvalidProxyURL` and catch it as an InvalidURL.

When evaluating Request.full_url (directly, or transitively via Request.send/path_url/response building), if the parsed netloc causes netloc.encode('idna') to raise a UnicodeError (e.g. an empty, too-long, or otherwise invalid IDNA label in an otherwise scheme-supported URL), the operation raises an InvalidURL exception carrying the message 'URL has an invalid label.' rather than letting the raw UnicodeError propagate out.
When max_gap is provided and is not a scalar (e.g. any array-like or list), interpolate_na raises ValueError with message 'max_gap must be a scalar.'

When set_index forms a MultiIndex (two or more source coordinates merged) onto a dimension d, every other variable of the object that was still dimensioned along one of the absorbed source-coordinate names (because that source coordinate had served as the variable's own dimension) has that dimension rewritten to the MultiIndex dimension d in the result; no retained variable keeps a dangling reference to a dimension name that has become a MultiIndex level.

AbstractArray.__format__ invoked with a non-empty format_spec on an array-valued (shape != ()) object raises NotImplementedError with a message stating that using format_spec is only supported when shape is () and reporting the actual shape.

Converting to a pandas.Index an xarray Variable or DataArray whose underlying data is a pandas MultiIndex stored at a particular level (i.e. a MultiIndex level coordinate, such as a named level 'one' of a stacked dimension) yields a single-level, non-Multi pandas.Index of that level's values repeated per position, rather than the underlying full pandas MultiIndex of row tuples.
pylint.constants defines DeletedMessage as a NamedTuple whose fields are 'msgid' (str), 'symbol' (str), and 'old_names' (a list of (str,str) pairs defaulting to the empty list).

The new 'glob_paths_csv' argument type transforms a comma-separated list of path entries by expanding user (~) and environment variables and then expanding glob patterns recursively on each entry, returning the concatenation of all matched paths in entry order so that an entry matching nothing contributes no path and an entry matching several paths contributes all of them (paths that name a literal existing file/dir still pass through).

Invoking the pylint Run entry point with no file/package arguments (and with --version / pylint-config command handling not otherwise short-circuiting) prints the single line "No files to lint: exiting." to stdout and exits with code 32, instead of printing the full linter help text.

Assertion rewriting now gives assignment expressions (the walrus operator `:=`, ast.NamedExpr on Python >= 3.8) a dedicated visitor: a walrus that is part of a rewritten assertion's test is turned into an assignment that is snapshotted and described in the assertion's introspection, so a failing assertion whose condition contains a walrus produces an explanation that references the walrus's bound value/name like an ordinary variable, instead of the walrus falling through to generic handling that rewrites/mis-renders it.

The new DatetimeFormatter formatter's formatTime(record, datefmt): when datefmt is non-empty and contains the '%f' directive, it returns the record's time rendered by datetime.strftime (which understands %f), substituting %f with a 6-digit microsecond field derived from the record's msecs attribute (its milliseconds converted to microseconds) within the record's local time & zone; when datefmt is empty or contains no '%f', formatTime(record, datefmt) returns exactly what the standard logging.Formatter.formatTime would return, so date formats without %f produce unchanged output.

get_feature_names raises a ValueError with message of form "input_features should have length equal to number of features ({n_features}), got {given_length}" when a supplied input_features has length differing from the number of input features (len(self.categories_)).

Calling LabelEncoder.inverse_transform with an empty (0-sample) input on a fitted encoder returns an empty numpy array (np.array([])) rather than proceeding through the unseen-label validation and array indexing.
Passing any explicit (non-None) axis value to the Imputer, including 0 or 1, causes fit to emit a DeprecationWarning announcing that 'axis' is deprecated in 0.20 and will be removed in 0.22.
Calling KNeighborsMixin.kneighbors with an explicit n_neighbors argument that is less than or equal to 0 raises a ValueError reporting the offending n_neighbors.

After `fit`, SimpleImputer sets an `indicator_` attribute: when add_indicator=True it is a fitted sklearn.impute.MissingIndicator instance constructed with the imputer's own `missing_values` placeholder and trained on the fit-time data; when add_indicator=False it is None.

In precision_recall_fscore_support with average='binary' and a binary target whose only present label is the negative class (requested pos_label is absent, so the positive class has zero true positives and zero true/predicted samples), the function no longer short-circuits to a silent literal (0., 0., 0., 0) tuple; instead it proceeds through the normal support/divide computation with labels=[pos_label], so the ill-defined positive-class metrics are reported as 0.0 and an UndefinedMetricWarning is raised rather than the call returning a hard-coded all-zero tuple with no warning.

When explicit categories are provided at fit, for each column whose own dtype is numerical (not object) the provided categories for that column, cast to that column's dtype, must be sorted — if they are not, fit raises ValueError('Unsorted categories are not supported for numerical categories'); object-dtype columns are exempt from this requirement regardless of the dtype of other columns in the same input.

When GradientBoosting.fit is called with an explicit sample_weight and the init estimator's fit (as happens with an sklearn Pipeline) raises a ValueError whose message contains 'not enough values to unpack', a ValueError is raised whose message is 'The initial estimator <init.__class__.__name__> does not support sample weights.', chained from the original ValueError

AffinityPropagation.fit(X, y) with affinity='precomputed' and X a scipy sparse matrix raises an error during input validation (check_array with accept_sparse=False), rather than accepting the sparse matrix and storing it as affinity_matrix_.

_euclidean_distances_upcast accepts an optional batch_size argument (in addition to X, XX, Y, YY). When batch_size is None, its chunk size is auto-derived from the X/Y sparsity-based memory heuristic as before; when a batch_size value is supplied, that value is taken directly as the chunk size for batching over both X rows and Y rows (skipping the auto memory-based computation) and the remaining per-X-chunk Y-batch iteration proceeds using that chunk size.

For any normalization mode, divisions that would otherwise yield NaN (arising from a zero row, zero column, or zero total sum) are replaced with 0 in the returned confusion_matrix, rather than being surfaced as NaN/Inf entries (division operations are carried out with runtime floating-point errors suppressed).

When an iterable fed to sklearn.utils.parallel.Parallel.__call__ contains a delayed function that does not support config attachment (e.g. one created with joblib.delayed instead of sklearn.utils.parallel.delayed), a UserWarning is raised stating that sklearn.utils.parallel.Parallel must be used in conjunction with sklearn.utils.parallel.delayed rather than joblib.delayed to correctly propagate the scikit-learn configuration; the task still runs without an attached shared config.

_get_n_samples_bootstrap, when given a float (Real) max_samples, returns a count of round(n_samples * max_samples) that is never below 1: if round(n_samples * max_samples) would be 0, the returned number of bootstrap samples is 1.

export_text accepts class_names given as any array-like (list, numpy array, and other array-like containers) of target-class labels; previously only a list was accepted. The provided names are used to label leaf classes in the returned report.

In BaseForest.fit, the unavailable-target check that raises ValueError ('The type of target cannot be used to compute OOB estimates...') for an OOB-unsupported y (multiclass-multioutput or unknown) is performed only when oob_score is set AND either new estimators were grown this call or the estimator lacks an oob_score_; a warm_start refit that grows no new trees on an already-OOB-computed estimator never raises this ValueError regardless of the supplied y's target type.

When PowerTransformer fits with method='box-cox' on data that contains a column (feature) consisting entirely of NaN values, the fit/fit_transform raises a ValueError (rather than attempting to compute the Box-Cox lambda on an empty non-NaN slice and failing with an unpacking error).

When the configured language is exactly 'en', Sphinx performs no catalog searching, mo-file compilation, or translator population from locale dirs (the translator is initialized with an empty locale list) and logs none of the 'loading translations...'/'done'/'not available for built-in messages' messages.

When rendering a `footnote` node that is tagged `referred` (i.e. it is referenced more than once, so the later references have been rewritten to `footnotemark` nodes by the LaTeXFootnoteTransform), the emitted LaTeX is a plain footnote environment that starts directly with `\begin{footnote}[<label>]\sphinxAtStartFootnote`, and the writer no longer prefixes that environment with a `\sphinxstepexplicit ` invocation and no longer inserts a `\phantomsection\label{\thesphinxscope.<label>}%` anchor (with its trailing comment-newline) inside the environment body.
`inherited_members_option(arg)` for a falsy argument that is not True/None (e.g. False or an empty string) returns the empty set, so no ancestor-name filtering is requested.
The mathjax_path configuration value, when not explicitly set by the user (i.e. left at its default), defaults to the string 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js'.

IndexEntries.create_index orders the top-level entries so that every symbol entry (an entry whose NFD-normalized, lowercased key with any leading right-to-left mark stripped does not begin with an alphabetic character or '_', e.g. entries starting with '£', '←', '&', or '@') sorts before every entry beginning with an alphabetic character or '_', regardless of the symbol's Unicode code point; consequently the returned grouped index contains its symbol entries in a single contiguous symbol group (keyed _('Symbols')) that appears first, before the alphabetical groups, instead of allowing non-ASCII symbols to sort after the letter entries and thereby emit a second, non-adjacent Symbols section.

Documenter.process_doc guarantees that, under an active app (self.env.app truthy), every non-empty docstring chunk it processes ends with exactly one trailing blank line: after the 'autodoc-process-docstring' event handlers have run (seeing the chunk without this added blank), if the chunk is non-empty and its last line is not the empty string '', a '' line is appended to the end of the chunk before its lines are yielded, and no extra blank line is added when the chunk is empty or already ends with ''.

The C domain DefinitionParser accepts as fundamental type specifiers the remaining GNU/standard-extension scalar keywords: the decimal '_Decimal32'/'_Decimal64'/'_Decimal128'; the integers '__uint128', '__int128', and (optionally 'signed'/'unsigned'-prefixed) '__int(8|16|32|64|128)'; and the floating/profile extensions '__float80', '_Float64x', '__float128', '_Float128', '__ibm128', '__fp16'.

restify(cls) returns a string argument unchanged (verbatim), so when cls is an instance of str the return value equals the input string itself; previously such an argument was not matched by the class-handling branches and resulted in its repr() (quoted form) being returned.

CCodePrinter now prints Relational expressions (Eq, Ne, Gt, Lt, Ge, Le) as an inline infix C comparison '<lhs_code> <rel_op> <rhs_code>' with the C operator token and surrounding spaces (for example 'x != 0', 'x == c') instead of falling back to StrPrinter's representation (which rendered == ' as 'Eq(...)' and '!=' as 'Ne(...)').

Arguments passed to _print_Or that bind less tightly than Or (e.g. nested conjunction operands) are wrapped in parentheses so disjunctions of conjunctions print e.g. '(x & ~y) | (y & ~x)' and disjunctions over multiple relationals print each <relational>-conjunction in parentheses, preserving the disjunction's operands as distinct grouped terms.

When factorint(n, multiple=True) yields a factorization in which an entry has non-positive multiplicity (a case reachable only when n's inputs introduce denominator primes, e.g. factor-rich Mul/dict composite inputs), that entry is represented in the returned list by S(1)/p repeated |multiplicity| times rather than by an integer p; otherwise positive-multiplicity entries remain integers p.

For a Function instance with a non-empty argument list, __new__ performs the automatic numeric evalf exactly when evaluate is enabled, the constructed object is an instance of the class, and every argument is one that should be auto-evalf'd (all return positive _should_evalf precision); in that case it returns the result numerically evaluated to a number of decimal places derived from the maximum argument precision. When evaluate is disabled, the object is not an instance of the class, or the instance has no arguments, no auto-evaluation occurs and the constructed result is returned as-is.

When expr is an Add expression and separate=True, decompose returns a Python set (unordered, duplicate-free) whose elements are the constituent monomials of expr (one per Add term), instead of a list.
For an argument z known to be real, sinh(z).is_positive equals z.is_positive (True iff z is positive real); for non-real z it is not asserted.

The negative-base, negative-exponent simplification in both Rational._eval_power and Integer._eval_power no longer branches on whether the negative exponent is an integer (expt.q == 1): a single representation is returned for all negative non-unit exponents, with the sign factored as (-1)**expt using the untransformed negative exponent.

In the unicode path of _print_BasisDependent, when reassembling a newline-containing coefficient, the branch that re-inserts the basis vector label is chosen by which parenthesis glyph the stripped coefficient text contains: if it contains the `\N{right parenthesis extension}` glyph (a vertically-extended/fraction-height rendering), the label is inserted exactly once immediately after the first occurrence of that glyph (the loop breaks after the first insertion), instead of being duplicated after every parenthesis hook on every line of the tall rendering.

In periodicity(f, symbol), when f is a Mod whose argument a is neither symbol itself nor a TrigonometricFunction, the linear-period shortcut returning Abs(n/a.diff(symbol)) is used only when a is a polynomial in symbol (and degree(a, symbol)==1 and symbol is not in the free symbols of the Mod modulus n); for a Mod argument a that is not a polynomial in symbol, this shortcut is no longer taken.

The differential operator text used is '∂' (partial) when requires_partial(e) is true and otherwise the total-differential value ('ⅆ'); the same operator selection applies consistently to the numerator and to every denominator operator as determined by the current hunk's unified 'd' variable.
For a power with a base known to be zero and an exponent known to be real, Pow.is_negative always returns False (a zero base to any real exponent is never negative).

When Factors is constructed from a general Expr (a non-atom, non-pure-Number product expression) whose resulting powers-dict contains a key f that is a non-Integer Rational p/q with exponent e (=factors[f]), the construction no longer keeps that Rational entry in Factors.factors; instead Integer(p) is entered/accumulated with exponent +e, Integer(q) is entered/accumulated with exponent -e, and the Rational key f is removed.

For a Segment3D or Ray3D argument whose intersection with the plane is empty (the entity does not reach the plane), Plane.distance returns the Euclidean distance from the plane to the nearest point actually on that bounded/ray entity rather than the perpendicular plane-to-point distance to that entity's first defining point regardless of its extent: for a Ray3D this is the plane-to-point distance of the ray's initial point o.p1, and for a Segment3D it is the plane-to-point distance of the nearer of the two endpoints.
calling isqrt with a negative argument raises ValueError (with message 'n must be nonnegative') rather than computing via the float/integer-nthroot path

Range accepts symbolic start/stop/step arguments (an argument that contains a Symbol and is not known to be non-integer, or is infinite) instead of raising ValueError; e.g. Range(i, j, k) with pure symbols constructs successfully and its .start/.stop/.step expose the supplied symbolic values (no literal-integer requirement). Finite literal non-integer arguments (e.g. pi) are still rejected with the 'Finite arguments to Range must be integers' ValueError.

When evaluating a reciprocal power (Pow(b, e))**other with e == -1 (i.e. an inner exponent of -1) and with `other` having a rational form whose denominator is literally 2 (the `_half` case), a base b that is known to be non-negative (b.is_negative is False) is simplified directly to `Pow(b, -other)` (i.e. b**-other) — e.g. computing (b**-1)**Rational(m,2) for such a b reduces to b**Rational(-m,2).
SchurNumber(S.Infinity) evaluates (via eval) to S.Infinity.

When uniq iterates over a seq whose length is determinable at call time (len(seq) succeeds and is recorded), if the seq is subsequently mutated during iteration so that its current length no longer equals the length recorded when uniq was called, iteration raises RuntimeError (whose message contains 'sequence changed size during iteration') instead of silently continuing with corrupted output; this detection applies on the normal hashable-element dedup path and on the unhashable-element (TypeError) fallback path.

The purestr representation of a MatrixSymbol built from a string name remains reconstructible: purestr(MatrixSymbol('x', 2, 2)) yields the exact code string 'MatrixSymbol(Str('x'), Integer(2), Integer(2))' whose eval equals the original MatrixSymbol (mirroring the documented behavior of dotprint/srepr output after the Str conversion).

In LatexPrinter._print_Pow, when the expression is a Pow whose base is a commutative Rational unit-fraction (base.p * base.q == abs(base.q)) and whose negative rational exponent is not -1, the LaTeX emitted is \frac{1}{(\frac{p}{q})^{m}} where p,q are the base's stored numerator/denominator and m is the absolute value of the negative exponent (e.g. rendering Pow(Rational(1,2), -2, evaluate=False) as '\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{2})^{2}}'), rather than routing through _print_Mul.

When Factors is constructed from an Expr whose power decomposition already has an entry keyed by the imaginary unit I and whose commutative argument list also contains standalone I atoms (whose count i was removed from the args), the resulting I entry in the factors dict is the sum of the pre-existing I-entry exponent and i — the pre-existing I exponent is not clobbered/replaced by i.

When a denominator-only unevaluated Mul has exactly one denominator factor, the printed numerator is the literal '1' and the result takes the single-factor form '1/<denominator>' (no enclosing parentheses); when it has more than one denominator factor the result takes the multi-factor form '1/(<d1>*<d2>...)' with parenthesized denominator.

UnitSystem._collect_factor_and_dimension still returns, as the factor (first) component of a Function expression, the expression's .func applied to the collected scale factors of its arguments (this wrapping of factors is unchanged); only the dimension component is no longer wrapped in the function.

When Quantity.__array_ufunc__ raises a TypeError or ValueError while handling a numpy ufunc and every one of the inputs and out arguments has a __array_ufunc__ that is only None, np.ndarray.__array_ufunc__, or Quantity.__array_ufunc__ (i.e., no genuinely custom override), the original exception is re-raised/propagated to the caller unchanged rather than being swallowed or converted to NotImplemented.

When SkyCoord.__getattr__ is invoked for an attribute that is not handled by its forwarding logic (not a matching frame alias/name, not a frame attribute, not present on the underlying _sky_coord_frame, and not a frame name transformable to), the object defers to normal attribute lookup (self.__getattribute__) so that the AttributeError ultimately raised is the standard one from Python's attribute machinery / the attribute's descriptor — with its own message — rather than replacing it with a SkyCoord-crafted generic attribute-error message; this applies equally whether the attribute is genuinely absent (yielding the standard "'...' object has no attribute '...'" error naming the object's actual class) or present via a subclass property/descriptor whose getter raises its own AttributeError (which now propagates unchanged instead of being swallowed).

CDS-format division of units is now left-associative: a CDS unit string containing two or more consecutive unparenthesised '/' separators groups them left to right, so that terms of the form U/V/W are parsed as (U/V)/W — physically U·V⁻¹·W⁻¹, with each unit after the first '/' ending up in the denominator — rather than the previous right-expansion U/(V/W). For example parsing 'J/m/s/kpc2' (or 'erg/cm2/s', etc.) with format='cds' yields the composite whose power vector assigns power −1 to m, s and kpc2, i.e. the base equivalent of J/(m·s·kpc2), instead of the old J/(m/(s/kpc2)) nesting.

When an Aggregate (e.g. a Count) is compiled to SQL with distinct=True, the rendered function arguments contain the keyword DISTINCT followed by whitespace, so it is separated from the leading source expression rather than being concatenated directly onto it (an expression whose SQL starts with a keyword- or identifier-like token, such as a CASE, previously merged with DISTINCT into a single invalid token). When distinct=False, no DISTINCT is emitted.

When FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS is left at its default and a FileSystemStorage is constructed without an explicit file_permissions_mode, a file saved through that storage is chmod'd to permission mode 0o644 after being stored (in both the file-move and streamed-write save paths), rather than retaining the source temp-file mode or the umask-derived creation mode.

Under Oracle, when USE_TZ is enabled, _convert_field_to_tz (used by datetime_cast_date_sql, datetime_cast_time_sql, datetime_extract_sql, and datetime_trunc_sql) treats the stored datetime field as being in the connection's configured timezone: when self.connection.timezone_name differs from the requested tzname the SQL takes the field as being in the connection timezone (FROM_TZ source = self.connection.timezone_name, replacing the fixed '0:00' UTC offset) and converts it to tzname, and when the two timezones are equal the field is returned unchanged without any conversion.

For an InlineModelAdmin on an auto-created M2M implicit through model, has_view_permission(request, obj) returns True if the request.user has either the 'view' or the 'change' permission on the target model (the model other than parent_model that the through model relates to); it no longer grants add/change/delete via that view check.

UUIDField.get_prep_value coerces input through UUIDField.to_python: a non-uuid.UUID string-hexadecimal or integer value is converted into the corresponding uuid.UUID instance (so that a call such as pk.get_prep_value(<string object_id>) yields a uuid.UUID comparable to a UUID primary-key value), an already-uuid.UUID value and None are returned unchanged, and an unparseable value raises the same ValidationError as to_python.

ModelChoiceField: When a ModelChoiceField uses a RadioSelect widget but the field does allow blank (blank argument is True), the leading empty/blank choice is retained (empty_label stays equal to the supplied empty_label, defaulting to '---------'), so an empty radio option is still rendered.

Query.output_field, when len(self.select) == 1 and the single select expression exposes a 'target' attribute that is truthy (e.g. a Col selecting a concrete column), returns that element's 'target' field rather than the element's own 'field'/output field.

SessionBase._legacy_encode returns an ASCII string that is base64-encoded content of hash.encode() + b':' + serialized, where serialized is self.serializer().dumps(session_dict) and hash is self._hash(serialized); the resulting string is in the legacy format consumed by _legacy_decode.

For every URL kwarg captured by a TemplateView, the value that _wrap_url_kwargs_with_deprecation_warning places into its returned mapping retains the deprecation contract: evaluating it as its underlying value triggers a RemovedInDjango40Warning whose message says TemplateView passing URL kwargs to the context is deprecated and instructs referencing the key through view.kwargs in the template, and yields the originally captured value.

When get_limit_choices_to() resolves to a falsy value (such as None or an empty mapping/dict), apply_limit_choices_to_to_formfield does not restrict the queryset — the form field keeps its original unfiltered queryset.

On backend connections whose JSON support is not native (connection.features.has_native_json_field is False), the rhs values of a key-transform __in lookup are not produced by the stock In rhs preparation alone; instead each candidate value is wrapped by an extraction function so that membership is checked against the decoded JSON key value.

When ordering two Field instances with equal creation_counters: an unattached field (no model) orders before a model-attached field; two fields both attached to models are ordered by comparing their models' (app_label, model_name) tuples; two unattached fields with equal counters are not strictly ordered relative to one another.

When display_for_field is called with a value that is truthy and a field that is a models.JSONField, the returned text is the JSON serialization of that value in which non-ASCII characters appear as literal characters rather than as \uXXXX escapes (serialized with python json.dumps using ensure_ascii=False and the field's encoder); on a serialization TypeError it still falls back to display_for_value(value, empty_value_display).

When a lazy proxy value appears on the LEFT-hand side of the addition operator (evaluated as ``<lazy_proxy> + <other>``), the lazy proxy is forced to its concrete value and the operation's result is ``<cast concrete value> + <other>`` (delegating to the concrete value's ``__add__``) rather than raising a TypeError.
Files that are not adjustable continue to be yielded immediately during the initial single post-processing pass (their results are not deferred to the end).

The `-m` relaunch branch is now selected based solely on __main__.__spec__ being present (not None); it is no longer additionally gated on a truthy __main__.__spec__.parent, so when __spec__ exists but parent is empty the child is still relaunched via `python -m <name>` rather than falling through to the script-file path.

When the value being serialized by TypeSerializer (via serializer_factory / MigrationWriter.serialize) is exactly the models.Model class type (identity match in the special_cases list), the serialization result is the string 'models.Model' with the import set {'from django.db import models'}, so that this import is propagated into the writer's imports and a generated migration referencing models.Model (e.g. as a CreateModel base) ends up importing models from django.db.

When the search term contains multiple words and search_fields includes a lookup that traverses a relation (e.g. a ForeignKey path), the per-word match criteria are combined into a single conjunction (one queryset.filter call over a single AND of the per-word OR query groups) rather than applying an independent filter per word — so the number of traversals/joins to the related model introduced by a multi-word search does not multiply with the number of words (each related search relation is exercised once for the whole term, not once per word).

Query.bump_prefix accepts an optional `exclude` iterable of aliases; when supplied, those aliases are left unchanged (not relabeled to the newly chosen prefix), while all other aliases are renumbered to fresh aliases under the new prefix. When `exclude` is None (the historical calling convention), every alias is relabeled as before.

When migrate() is invoked with an explicit empty plan (plan == []) and the django_migrations table does not exist on the migration connection's database, migrate() returns the ProjectState built from the unmigrated apps (with_applied_migrations=False) without creating the django_migrations table (i.e. it performs an early return before ensure_schema/table creation and before folding applied migrations into the state).

When adding a field whose primary_key is True to an existing model on SQLite, DatabaseSchemaEditor.add_field uses the full table-remake procedure (_remake_table, which rebuilds the table) rather than a plain 'ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN', so the new primary-key column/semantics are realized on the rebuilt table rather than attempted via unsupported inline ALTER.

The base Field class exposes a per-field-class attribute `non_db_attrs` (a tuple of attribute names whose change does not affect a column definition and thus is ignored when deciding whether a field alteration is needed). Its default value includes blank, choices, db_column, editable, error_messages, help_text, limit_choices_to, on_delete, related_name, related_query_name, validators, and verbose_name; standard field subclasses inherit it. A custom field subclass may override/extend `non_db_attrs` to declare which of its deconstruct keyword attributes are non-schema-affecting.

get_template_directories() skips any falsy/empty-string directory returned by a template loader's get_dirs() (it only considers non-empty directories that are not Django paths), so such an entry does not cause Path.cwd() to be added to the returned set of template directories.

ForeignKey.db_parameters(connection) returns a dict that, in addition to 'type' and 'check', contains a 'collation' key whose value is the value returned under 'collation' by the foreign key's target_field.db_parameters(connection).

When RenameIndex.database_forwards resolves the pre-renaming (from-state / actually-present) index and that index's name already equals self.new_name — i.e. the operation is a no-op because nothing would change — it performs no database schema change (does not call schema_editor.rename_index, and does not require the to_state index lookup) and returns normally, rather than attempting to rename an index to a name it already carries (which previously triggered a duplicate-relation error on re-application of an unnamed-index rename after its no-op backward step).

When the schema editor removes a unique_together (deleted set in alter_unique_together processed through _delete_composed_index), it locates the database constraint to drop by filtering to constraints that are unique and are NOT primary keys. As a result, for a model whose removed unique_together field set is also (or includes) the primary key on a backend whose introspection reports that primary-key constraint as unique=True, the removal no longer counts the primary key as one of the matching unique constraints and therefore no longer raises "Found wrong number (...)"; it drops only the actual unique constraint and leaves the primary key intact.

When a defer()/only() column spec traverses an intermediate relation whose target model is a proxy model, Query.deferred_to_data registers the required pk/reference fields under the proxy's concrete backing model (so the concrete model's pk column is included among the selected/loaded columns), and the resulting query loads and populates the related (proxy) object with its pk correctly set rather than failing during object population because the pk column is missing.

A `%` (MOD connector) CombinedExpression whose operands are an Integer output field and a Float output field (in either order) no longer raises FieldError during output-field resolution; its inferred output type is FloatField.

SelectDateWidget.value_from_datadict does not raise OverflowError when the submitted year/month/day values are integers that cause datetime.date(int(y), int(m), int(d)) to raise OverflowError (rather than ValueError); instead it returns the string "0-0-0".

The above cancellation matches purely on the index name (self.index.name == operation.name) without constraining that the paired RemoveIndex targets the same model as the AddIndex or that it immediately follows it, so an AddIndex is also cancelled by a RemoveIndex naming that index even when the two operations name different models and/or have other operations in between.

Calling Axes.set_xlim with a reversed (descending) request on a log-scaled x-axis — e.g. ax.set_xlim(x_max, x_min) where the first argument > the second — produces an inverted (descending) x view interval instead of being silently re-sorted ascending by log-scale limit adjustment: afterwards get_xlim()/viewLim.intervalx returns its two values with the first greater than the second and ax.xaxis_inverted() == True. Normal ascending calls (first argument < second) still yield a non-inverted ascending interval.

When an interactive (interactive=True) vertical SpanSelector is created, the two initial edge-handle artist lines are placed at data y-positions equal to the axes' current y-axis data limits (ax.get_ybound()), rather than at the initially-zero selector extents; consequently constructing the selector leaves the axes' y view limits unchanged (does not autoscale them, in particular does not expand them toward data coordinate 0 when 0 lies outside the data view).

The align grouping in _get_aligned_offsets now pairs 'left' with 'bottom' (both on the offsets=[d,...] / descent-side branch) and 'right' with 'top' (both on the offsets=[height-h+d,...] branch), so that align='top' behaves like align='right' and align='bottom' behaves like align='left' within the shared helper.

AnnotationBbox.draw invokes renderer.open_group with self.__class__.__name__ as the group title (no type name string literal required beyond that source constant being reflected) before drawing its children when it proceeds past the visibility/xy guards.

When contourf()/QuadContourSet (filled=True) is drawn from a Z whose dtype is boolean and no contour levels are supplied, automatic level selection uses levels [0, 0.5, 1], so the resulting cs.levels equal [0, 0.5, 1].

Constructing an OffsetFrom from a ref_coord that is a numpy array does not alias the caller's array: OffsetFrom stores a value copy of ref_coord, so that later in-place mutation of the passed ref_coord array after construction does not affect the offset transform returned by OffsetFrom.__call__.
When prepare_content_length is called with body=None on a request whose method is neither 'GET' nor 'HEAD' (e.g. POST), the 'Content-Length' header is still set to '0'.

Dataset.merge(other) now accepts a xarray.DataArray as `other` by first converting it to a Dataset via other.to_dataset() before delegating to dataset_merge_method; consequently the DataArray's named data variable and coordinates participate in the merge rather than an AttributeError being raised. (For an unnamed DataArray, to_dataset raises ValueError, so Dataset.merge with an unnamed DataArray raises ValueError rather than AttributeError.)

Indexing a DataArray by label through .loc with a dict-like key (e.g. da.loc[{dim: label}]) returns the DataArray produced by selecting on those dimension labels, treating every dict key as a dimension/coordinate to look up rather than as a Python keyword argument — so this works correctly even when a dimension (or a key in the indexers dict) is named 'method', 'tolerance', 'drop', or 'indexers', which are reserved parameter names of DataArray.sel.

IndexVariable.to_index_variable() (and its to_coord alias) returns a new IndexVariable object that is distinct from the receiver rather than returning the receiver itself, so that mutating the returned variable (e.g. assigning its dims) does not change the dims of the IndexVariable it was called on.

In the dot (.dot) class diagram emitted by DotWriter.get_values / write_classes, each displayed method whose signature declares a type annotation on a positional argument other than `self` is rendered with that annotation as `methodname(argname: Type)`, pairing each annotation to its argument positionally; arguments without an annotation are rendered bare `argname` (multiple arguments joined by ', ').

When a RidgeClassifierCV is constructed with both cv set to a non-None value and store_cv_values=True, calling fit(X, y) raises a ValueError indicating that cv!=None and store_cv_values=True are incompatible.

When the search is run with a falsy `refit` (i.e. `refit=False`), calling fit does not create a `refit_time_` attribute on the instance, so the attribute is absent after fit (accessing it raises AttributeError).

The single effective copy_X value resolved for a LassoLarsIC.fit call (explicit argument if given, else the estimator's copy_X attribute) is applied consistently to both the data preprocessing step (LinearModel._preprocess_data) and the lars_path call, so that whether the caller's input X array is copied or modified in place is governed by that one resolved value rather than being split between the two.

In StratifiedKFold._make_test_folds, self.random_state is normalized through check_random_state into a concrete random number generator exactly once before any per-class split is produced; that single generator (whose state advances) is shared by the per-class KFold splitting kernels. As a result, for shuffle=True with an integer random_state, the shuffling of different classes comes from successive draws of the one seed-derived stream rather than each class independently re-seeding and re-deriving an identical permutation from the integer.

HuberRegressor.fit accepts an input feature matrix X whose dtype is non-float (e.g. integer or boolean/categorical data stored as bool), casting it internally to a floating-point dtype and fitting successfully, so that calling fit does not raise a TypeError originating from numpy operations on the non-float array and the resulting model behaves equivalently to one fit on the same data converted to float64/float32.

export_text(decision_tree, feature_names=...) builds its internal per-node feature-name list by mapping split-node feature indices to the corresponding provided feature_names entries, while never using the TREE_UNDEFINED sentinel that leaf nodes store as an index into feature_names, so that calling export_text with a single-feature tree (whose leaf nodes store feature == TREE_UNDEFINED == -2) and a length-1 feature_names list completes and returns the text report instead of raising IndexError.

Under the refit=False (aggregation) path of LogisticRegressionCV.fit, when the penalty is not 'elasticnet', each class entry appended to self.l1_ratio_ is the value None (rather than being derived by indexing the internally-degenerate l1_ratios grid, which for non-elasticnet is the single-element [None] used as a dummy). Observable consequence: after fitting a non-elasticnet LogisticRegressionCV with refit=False, self.l1_ratio_ holds None values, matching the refit=True behavior.

In cluster_optics_xi, when a min_cluster_size that is not None is given as a fraction in (0, 1], it is rescaled to max(2, int(min_cluster_size * n_samples)) — the fractional product truncated to an integer with a floor of 2 — rather than remaining a float.

IterativeImputer's constructor accepts a keyword-only parameter `fill_value` that defaults to `None`, and the value passed is stored in the estimator's `fill_value` attribute, so that e.g. `IterativeImputer(fill_value=X).fill_value == X` and `get_params()` exposes it as such.

When building the diagram's URL map in html_visit_inheritance_diagram from a resolved class reference (a pending_xref child carrying a 'refuri'): an external intersphinx reference (child with 'internal' falsy, i.e. not default/true) is recorded under the key equal to the substring of the refuri that follows its final '#', while an internal refuri-based reference is recorded under the key equal to its 'reftitle'.

The source text argument delivered to a 'source-read' handler for included RST content is the included file's actual content — its lines joined with ' ' — excluding the two trailing marker/sentinel lines that docutils (>=0.18) appends to the include input; after the handler returns, the possibly-modified text is re-split into lines and those two marker lines are re-attached so that parsing of the included content continues identically to before the handler ran.

The std domain's ':term:' cross-reference role no longer lowercases its reference text before use, so the term reference target stored on the pending_xref node (and matched against registered glossary terms) preserves the exact capitalization written in the reference instead of being case-folded.
sphinx.pycode.ast.unparse() on an AST Tuple node whose elts list is empty returns the string '()' rather than the empty string that would result from joining zero element strings.

For a non-http(s), non-'scheme://' link URI whose srcdir-relative file does NOT exist on disk but that matches one of the configured linkcheck_ignore patterns, the linkcheck builder reports status 'ignored' (no network request) instead of 'local'.

When an automodule or autoclass directive is processed, the members explicitly named in a list-valued :private-members: or :special-members: option that are not already in the directive's :members: list are appended to it (so they are selected for member enumeration); this merging is skipped when :members: is given as a bare flag (ALL), and it happens both for ModuleDocumenter and ClassDocumenter.

For Python object descriptions, the argument (variable name) of a :var:, :ivar:, or :cvar: doc field is rendered as plain literal bold text rather than as a cross-reference of role 'obj'; it no longer produces a pending cross-reference that would be resolved against module- and/or class-scoped Python objects bearing that name, and it is therefore never resolved to a same-named object of unrelated scope nor reported as a missing reference under nitpicky builds.

In the described-only/typehints-description-target merge path (augment_descriptions_with_types), a docutils field whose extracted name is ':returns:' (parts[0] == 'returns') is recognized as describing the function's return value, exactly as a ':return:' field is.

Permutation.__new__ still rejects array-form entry containing repeated elements by raising ValueError('there were repeated elements.'); the repeated-element rejection is now applied only when the permutation is not in cyclic form.

When an object that is already an instance of the requested class is passed to the constructor with an explicit size different from its own, the result is a new instance of that same class (subclass preserved) resized to the given size.

When mul_symbol is a custom string whose content is whitespace/empty once stripped, or is one of the LaTeX spacing commands r'\,', r'\:', r'\;', r'\quad', or a lone backslash r'\', the number-separator used when printing floats (mantissa-exponent form) and between adjacent numeric terms is the dot symbol (r' \cdot ') rather than the literal custom string.

Add.is_zero (the _eval_is_zero handler) returns None rather than False for an Add belonging to a commutative (real-valued or complex-valued sum) whose classified arguments contain no real term known to be nonzero but contain at least one imaginary-direction term (an argument with is_imaginary, or whose product with the imaginary unit I is real), with any real arguments being individually known-zero; i.e. an expression whose real part is established as zero but whose full zero-ness (whether the imaginary part cancels) is not decidable is reported as unknown (None), not as nonzero (False).

When posify replaces a free symbol whose positivity is unknown with a positive dummy, the dummy carries over all of that symbol's other explicit assumptions (not only positive=True); consequently, querying the returned expression's replacement symbol for any of the original symbol's explicit assumptions (e.g., finite) yields the same truth value as on the original symbol, and likewise for other declared assumptions such as integer/rational/odd/even.

The LaTeX rendering of a Subs expression always encloses the substituted expression (the LaTeX of subs.args[0], the expr being evaluated) in literal \left( ... \right) delimiters, so the emitted form is `\left. \left(<expr>\right) \right|_{\substack{ ... }}` regardless of what expr is.

After the removal step triggered by a newly found minimal block system, the set of block systems retained for comparison against subsequent candidates (and ultimately returned) is exactly the previously recorded systems that were not subsumed by the new candidate, so all systems rendered non-minimal (not merely the first one encountered) are dropped and none is dropped spuriously.

Equality/identity evaluation between two generic Set instances (the multiple-dispatch _eval_is_eq rule matched when neither operand has a more-specific handler) is determined by mutual subsethood: it resolves to (the fuzzy logic of) whether lhs.is_subset(rhs) AND rhs.is_subset(lhs) are both true, in place of the previous blanket 'None' answer that left such equalities unevaluated.

Declaring __slots__=() on the Printable mixin renders instances of Printable's slot-declaring subclasses (previously, since Printable lacked __slots__, any class whose MRO passed through Printable implicitly gained an instance __dict__) __slots__-only: a Symbol instance (and any instance of a Printable-derived class that itself defines __slots__) has no instance __dict__ — accessing its __dict__ either returns absent/raises AttributeError, and assigning a new, non-slot attribute to such an instance raises AttributeError rather than silently storing it in a __dict__.

split_super_sub still applies its trailing-digit exception when the given base name consists of one or more alphabetic characters immediately followed by a run of one or more digits: those trailing digits are removed from the returned name and prepended as the first element of the returned subs list. The alphabetic-prefix character condition is now Unicode-letter based ([^\W\d_], i.e. any non-digit, non-underscore word character), so the exception also fires for names whose letters include non-ASCII/Unicode characters (e.g. Greek), not just ASCII a-z/A-Z.

In _print_Mul's unequal-fraction handling, a commutative denominator factor that is a Pow whose exponent is exactly -1 and whose base has more than one argument is parenthesized in the printed output when that base is itself a Pow (e.g. base = a**b), the same way bases that are a Mul already are. Concretely, an unevaluated product such as Mul(x, Pow(a**b, -1, evaluate=False)) prints its denominator 'a**b' wrapped in parentheses rather than unwrapped, so the affected term appears with surrounding parentheses in the rendered string.

In CodePrinter._print_Mul, when an expression has a clearly-negative leading coefficient (sign '-') and its numerator reduces to exactly one factor, that lone factor is parenthesized against a weight strictly between PRECEDENCE['Mul'] and PRECEDENCE['Pow'] (0.5*(PRECEDENCE['Pow']+PRECEDENCE['Mul'])) rather than against the (Add-level) precedence of the negative Mul itself; consequently such a lone factor whose own precedence is below Pow-level (e.g. a Mul-level object) is now emitted inside parentheses directly after the leading '-'.

The plain (non-mod-D) ZZ Hermite-normal-form computation steps through all rows of the matrix from bottom to top, not merely the bottom min(m, n) rows, and stops only once a pivot occupies every one of the n columns. Consequently, for an integer matrix with more rows than columns (m > n) whose genuinely nonzero row(s) lie above the bottom min(m, n) rows, the returned HNF keeps columns holding nonzero pivots obtained from those upper rows rather than returning a column-stripped (empty-column) result that discards them; e.g. hermite_normal_form of a ZZ matrix such as [[2,7],[0,0],[0,0]] returns a result retaining the top row's pivot column instead of an empty 3x0 result.
Contains(x, S).as_set() returns S (the set given as the second argument of the Contains) instead of raising NotImplementedError.

When parse_expr is called with evaluate=False, an expression containing the Python '<=' comparison operator is parsed into an unevaluated instance of the SymPy relational class Le (Le(visited_left, visited_right, evaluate=False)) with the parsed operands, rather than being eagerly evaluated to a boolean.
